## Installation

You have to install both `@ahaui/react` and `@ahaui/css`

```sh
# With npm
npm install @ahaui/react @ahaui/css

# Or with yarn
yarn add @ahaui/react @ahaui/css
```

# gatsby-plugin-sorted-assets

A workaround for gatsby not sorting order-dependent assets, like css, in it's html building.

This should be moved to gatsby core, there is a pending PR to do so.

<h3 align="center">Aha Design System - Documentation</h3>

## Status

![Website](https://img.shields.io/website?url=https%3A%2F%2Fahaui.github.io&label=Documentation)

## Quick start

Aha's documentation is built with Gatsby and publicly hosted at https://ahaui.github.io/. The docs may also be run locally.

### Running documentation locally

0. Use `yarn` to install the Node.js dependencies
1. Clone this repository: `git clone git@github.com:gotitinc/ahaui.git`
4. `yarn install`
5. `yarn dev`
6. Open `http://localhost:8000/` in your browser.

## Copyright and license

AhaUI-Documentation is licensed under the [Apache-2.0 License](https://github.com/gotitinc/ahaui/blob/main/LICENSE), sponsored and supported by [Got It, Inc.](https://www.got-it.co).

# Accordion

Source: https://github.com/tutoruniverse/ahaui/blob/main/apps/docs/src/pages/components/accordion.mdx

title: Accordion
import ComponentApi from 'src/components/ComponentApi';
import customToggle from 'src/examples/Accordion/customToggle';
import togglePrimary from 'src/examples/Accordion/togglePrimary';
import toggleSecondary from 'src/examples/Accordion/toggleSecondary';
import toggleOutline from 'src/examples/Accordion/toggleOutline';
import exampleCollapse from 'src/examples/Accordion/exampleCollapse';

# Accordion

## Introduction

Using the default `<Collapse>` behavior to create an accordion. The collapse is used to show and hide content. With a few classes, buttons or anchors are used as triggers that are mapped to specific toggle elements.

The accordion component is created by extending the default collapse behavior. It's used to toggle the visibility of content.

Using accordion to display the content of Claim, Skip and Flag actions in bidding screens, or display the frequently asked questions (FAQs).

<img
  className="u-maxWidthFull"
  src={require('src/assets/structure/stb_accordion-structure.jpg')}
  srcSet={`${require('src/assets/structure/stb_accordion-structure@2x.jpg')} 2x`}
  alt="Accordion structure"
 <ol className="u-paddingLeftLarge u-textGray u-marginTopTiny">
  <li>
    Toggle Header&nbsp;
    <i className="u-text200">- Used as triggers that mapped to specific toggle elements.</i>
  </li>
  <li>
    Card Body&nbsp;
    <i className="u-text200">- The content inside the card body is flexible.</i>
  </li>
</ol>

## Examples

### Custom Toggle Header

Often used to the frequently asked questions to display a question in toggle header and an answer in the card body.

<CodeView codeText={customToggle}/>

### Button Toggle Header

Using similar design as a button, this example used to displays the content and shows more information about actions.

#### Primary
<CodeView codeText={togglePrimary}/>

#### Secondary

<CodeView codeText={toggleSecondary}/>

#### White outline

<CodeView codeText={toggleOutline} />

### Collapse

<CodeView codeText={exampleCollapse} />

## Design Reference
Two or more primary accordion components should not be placed next to each other. Different than a primary accordion component, two or more secondary accordion components can be used in one layout.
<div className="Grid u-marginBottomLarge">
  <div className="u-sizeFull md:u-size1of2">
    <img
      className="u-maxWidthFull"
      src={require('src/assets/ref/accordion-structure-do.jpg')}
      srcSet={`${require('src/assets/ref/accordion-structure-do@2x.jpg')} 2x`}
      alt="Accordion Do"
    <div className="u-borderBottom u-borderLarge u-borderPositive u-marginTopSmall" />
    <div className="u-textPositive">Do</div>
  </div>
  <div className="u-sizeFull md:u-size1of2">
    <img
      className="u-maxWidthFull"
      src={require('src/assets/ref/accordion-structure-dont.jpg')}
      srcSet={`${require('src/assets/ref/accordion-structure-dont@2x.jpg')} 2x`}
      alt="Accordion Dont"
    <div className="u-borderBottom u-borderLarge u-borderNegative u-marginTopSmall" />
    <div className="u-textNegative">Don't</div>
  </div>
</div>

## API

<ComponentApi metadata={props.data.Accordion} />
<ComponentApi metadata={props.data.AccordionToggle} exportedBy={props.data.Accordion} />
<ComponentApi metadata={props.data.AccordionCollapse} exportedBy={props.data.Accordion} />
<ComponentApi metadata={props.data.Collapse} />

### useAccordionToggle

```jsx
import { useAccordionToggle } from '@ahaui/react';

const decoratedOnClick = useAccordionToggle(eventKey, onClick);

```

export const query = graphql`
  query AccordionQuery {
    Accordion: componentMetadata(displayName: { eq: "Accordion" }) {
      ...ComponentApi_metadata
    AccordionToggle: componentMetadata(displayName: { eq: "AccordionToggle" }) {
      ...ComponentApi_metadata
    AccordionCollapse: componentMetadata(displayName: { eq: "AccordionCollapse" }) {
      ...ComponentApi_metadata
    Collapse: componentMetadata(displayName: { eq: "Collapse" }) {
      ...ComponentApi_metadata

# Avatars

Source: https://github.com/tutoruniverse/ahaui/blob/main/apps/docs/src/pages/components/avatars.mdx

title: Avatars

import ComponentApi from 'src/components/ComponentApi';
import photoAvatar from 'src/examples/Avatars/photo';
import sizesAvatar from 'src/examples/Avatars/size';
import textsAvatar from 'src/examples/Avatars/text';

# Avatars

## Introduction
An avatar is a circular component, which is used to represent people (askers & experts) and objects (system). Avatars can be photos, illustrations or icons.

## Examples

### Variants

#### Photo avatar
Uploaded by users. When an image hasn't been uploaded, the default avatar will be used.

<CodeView codeText={photoAvatar} />

#### Text avatar

<CodeView codeText={textsAvatar} />

#### Sizes

The following are the available sizes of the avatars:

<CodeView codeText={sizesAvatar} />

## Design Reference

N/A

## API

<ComponentApi metadata={props.data.metadata} />

export const query = graphql`
  query AvatarQuery {
    metadata: componentMetadata(displayName: { eq: "Avatar" }) {
      displayName
      ...ComponentApi_metadata

# Badges

# Badges

## Introduction

A badge contains a status or a numeric value, to indicate a running tally or quantity-based summary.
<img
  className="u-maxWidthFull"
  src={require('src/assets/structure/stb_badge-structure.jpg')}
  srcSet={`${require('src/assets/structure/stb_badge-structure@2x.jpg')} 2x`}
  alt="Badge structure"
<ol className="u-paddingLeftLarge u-textGray u-marginTopTiny">
  <li>Background</li>
  <li>Text</li>
</ol>

## Examples

### Variants

#### Subtle Style

Designed by lighter color, subtle badges are used for less important information.

<CodeView codeText={BadgeSubtle} transparentBackground />

#### Bold Style

Designed by lighter color, bold badges are used for important information.

<CodeView codeText={BadgeBold} transparentBackground />

## Design Reference
N/A

## API

<ComponentApi metadata={props.data.metadata} />

export const query = graphql`
  query BadgeQuery {
    metadata: componentMetadata(displayName: { eq: "Badge" }) {
      displayName
      ...ComponentApi_metadata

# Breadcrumb

Source: https://github.com/tutoruniverse/ahaui/blob/main/apps/docs/src/pages/components/breadcrumb.mdx

title: Breadcrumb
import ComponentApi from 'src/components/ComponentApi';
import defaultBreadcrumb from 'src/examples/Breadcrumb/default';
import schemaBreadcrumb from 'src/examples/Breadcrumb/schema';

# Breadcrumb

## Introduction

Indicate the current page’s location within a navigational hierarchy.
<img
  src={require('src/assets/structure/stb_breadcrumb-structure.jpg')}
  srcSet={`${require('src/assets/structure/stb_breadcrumb-structure@2x.jpg')} 2x`}
  alt="Breadcrumb structure"
<ol className="u-textGray u-marginTopTiny">
  <li>
      Breadcrumb items
    <i className="u-text200"> - Indicates pages in hierarchical order. Items are basically button links, except for the current page item.</i>
  </li>
  <li>
      Separator
    <i className="u-text200"> - Icon which is used to separate items.</i>
  </li>
</ol>

## Examples

<CodeView codeText={defaultBreadcrumb} />
<CodeView codeText={schemaBreadcrumb} />

## Design Reference

Don’t use breadcrumbs for top-level or single-level pages.

<div className="Grid u-marginBottomLarge">
  <div className="u-sizeFull md:u-size1of2">
    <img
      className="u-maxWidthFull"
      src={require('src/assets/ref/breadcrumb-structure-dont.jpg')}
      srcSet={`${require('src/assets/ref/breadcrumb-structure-dont@2x.jpg')} 2x`}
      alt="Breadcrumb Dont"
    <div className="u-borderBottom u-borderLarge u-borderNegative u-marginTopSmall" />
    <div className="u-textNegative">Don't</div>
  </div>
</div>

## API

<ComponentApi metadata={props.data.Breadcrumb} />
<ComponentApi metadata={props.data.BreadcrumbItem} exportedBy={props.data.Breadcrumb}/>

export const query = graphql`
  query BreadcrumbQuery {
    Breadcrumb: componentMetadata(displayName: { eq: "Breadcrumb" }) {
      ...ComponentApi_metadata
    BreadcrumbItem: componentMetadata(displayName: { eq: "BreadcrumbItem" }) {
      ...ComponentApi_metadata

# Bubble Chat

Source: https://github.com/tutoruniverse/ahaui/blob/main/apps/docs/src/pages/components/bubble-chat.mdx

title: Bubble Chat
import ComponentApi from 'src/components/ComponentApi';
import textMessageBubbleChat from 'src/examples/BubbleChat/textMessage';
import fileMessageBubbleChat from 'src/examples/BubbleChat/fileMessage';
import typingMessageBubbleChat from 'src/examples/BubbleChat/typingMessage';
import senderMessageBubbleChat from 'src/examples/BubbleChat/senderMessage';
import reviserMessageBubbleChat from 'src/examples/BubbleChat/reviserMessage';
import systemMessageBubbleChat from 'src/examples/BubbleChat/systemMessage';
import imageMessageBubbleChat from 'src/examples/BubbleChat/imageMessage';

# Bubble Chat

## Introduction

The component is used to represent the real-time and archived messages of three main objects: users, experts and system.

<img
  src={require('src/assets/structure/stb_bubble-chat-structure.jpg')}
  srcSet={`${require('src/assets/structure/stb_bubble-chat-structure@2x.jpg')} 2x`}
  alt="Bubble Chat"
<ol className="u-textGray u-marginTopTiny">
  <li>
    Message background
  </li>
  <li>Message content</li>
  <li>Avatar</li>
  <li>Time stamp</li>
</ol>

## Examples

### Text Message

<CodeView codeText={textMessageBubbleChat} />

### File Message

<CodeView codeText={fileMessageBubbleChat} />

### Image Message

<CodeView codeText={imageMessageBubbleChat} />

### Typing Message

<CodeView codeText={typingMessageBubbleChat} />

### Outbound Message

Normally this style is applied for users. Outbound messages use the system’s primary color and right-aligned.

<CodeView codeText={senderMessageBubbleChat} />

### Inbound Message

Normally this style is applied for experts. Inbound messages use the system’s secondary color, left-aligned and have an avatar on the left.

<CodeView codeText={reviserMessageBubbleChat} />

### System Message

System messages use the system’s primary-light color, left-aligned and have products’ avatars on the left.

<CodeView codeText={systemMessageBubbleChat} />

### Variants

**Light**
<CodeView codeText={`<div style={{ maxWidth: 360 }}>
  <BubbleChat
    variant="light"
    type="outbound"
    avatar={(() => <Avatar size="small" className="u-backgroundPrimaryLighter u-textPrimary u-text100" text="KT" />)}
    text="Welcome to Aha Design System"
    time="16:23"
</div>`} />

**Primary**
<CodeView codeText={`<div style={{ maxWidth: 360 }}>
  <BubbleChat
    variant="primary"
    type="outbound"
    avatar={(() => <Avatar size="small" className="u-backgroundPrimaryLighter u-textPrimary u-text100" text="KT" />)}
    text="Welcome to Aha Design System"
    time="16:23"
</div>`} />

**PrimaryLight**
<CodeView codeText={`<div style={{ maxWidth: 360 }}>
  <BubbleChat
    variant="primaryLight"
    type="outbound"
    avatar={(() => <Avatar size="small" className="u-backgroundPrimaryLighter u-textPrimary u-text100" text="KT" />)}
    text="Welcome to Aha Design System"
    time="16:23"
</div>`} />

**Dark**
<CodeView codeText={`<div style={{ maxWidth: 360 }}>
  <BubbleChat
    variant="dark"
    type="outbound"
    avatar={(() => <Avatar size="small" className="u-backgroundPrimaryLighter u-textPrimary u-text100" text="KT" />)}
    text="Welcome to Aha Design System"
    time="16:23"
</div>`} />

**TransparentDark**
<CodeView exampleClassName="u-backgroundDark" codeText={`<div style={{ maxWidth: 360 }}>
  <BubbleChat
    variant="transparentDark"
    type="outbound"
    avatar={(() => <Avatar size="small" className="u-backgroundPrimaryLighter u-textPrimary u-text100" text="KT" />)}

    time="16:23"
</div>`} />

**TransparentLight**
<CodeView codeText={`<div style={{ maxWidth: 360 }}>
  <BubbleChat

# Buttons

Source: https://github.com/tutoruniverse/ahaui/blob/main/apps/docs/src/pages/components/buttons.mdx

title: Buttons
import ComponentApi from 'src/components/ComponentApi';
import { Button } from '@ahaui/react';
import sizesButton from 'src/examples/Button/size';
import widthDefault from 'src/examples/Button/widthDefault';
import brandMicrosoft from 'src/examples/Button/brandMicrosoft';
import brandGoogle from 'src/examples/Button/brandGoogle';
import groupStylesButton from 'src/examples/Button/groupStyles';
import groupIconsButton from 'src/examples/Button/groupIcons';
import groupSizesButton from 'src/examples/Button/groupSizes';

# Buttons

## Introduction

A button is a clickable item used to execute an action either in the background or foreground.

<img
  className="u-maxWidthFull"
  src={require('src/assets/structure/stb_button-structure.jpg')}
  srcSet={`${require('src/assets/structure/stb_button-structure@2x.jpg')} 2x`}
  alt="Button structure"
<ol className="u-paddingLeftLarge u-textGray u-marginTopTiny">
  <li>
      Button text
  </li>
  <li>
      Left icon
  </li>
  <li>
      Right icon
  </li>
  <li>
      Text underline&nbsp;
    <i className="u-text200">- The underline is used for button link hover state.</i>
  </li>
  <li>
      Border
  </li>
  <li>
      Background
  </li>
  <li>
      Focus border
  </li>
</ol>

## Examples

### Variants

**Primary**

Most of the time, a primary button is used when the consequent action is the main action of a layout.

<CodeView codeText={`<Button variant="primary">
  <Button.Label>Button</Button.Label>
</Button>`}

**Secondary**

Secondary buttons are used to indicate supplementary actions

<CodeView codeText={`<Button variant="secondary">
  <Button.Label>Button</Button.Label>
</Button>`}

**Primary Outline**

A primary outline button is used when the consequent action is considered less important than the primary button but more important than the secondary button.

<CodeView codeText={`<Button variant="primary_outline">
  <Button.Label>Button</Button.Label>
</Button>`}

**Accent**

On some specific layouts (i.e. ask flow or payment), accent buttons overrule the primary buttons to indicate the most important actions.

<CodeView codeText={`<Button variant="accent">
  <Button.Label>Button</Button.Label>
</Button>`}

**Positive**

Positive buttons are used for positive actions (i.e. when users finish a flow). They can be used to update the positive status of an action in view-only mode.

<CodeView codeText={`<Button variant="positive">
  <Button.Label>Button</Button.Label>
</Button>`}

**Negative**

Negative buttons are used for negative actions (i.e. when users quit or stop an important flow).
<CodeView codeText={`<Button variant="negative">
  <Button.Label>Button</Button.Label>
</Button>`}

**White**

Using it as a primary button in color or dark background.
<CodeView
  transparentBackground
  codeText={`<Button variant="white">
  <Button.Label>Button</Button.Label>
</Button>`}

**White Ouline**

Using it as a secondary button in color or dark background.
<CodeView
  exampleClassName="u-backgroundDark"
  codeText={`<Button variant="white_outline">
  <Button.Label>Button</Button.Label>
</Button>`}

**Link**

The button link is the least prominent button. It's often standing next to other buttons to indicate a less important action.

Having paddings, a button link is different, and also, represents a more important action than a text link.
<CodeView
  transparentBackground
  codeText={`<Button as={SafeAnchor} href="https://designsystem.got-it.io/" variant="link">
  <Button.Label>Button</Button.Label>
</Button>`}

### States

**Disabled**

Disabled buttons allow users to know the consequent actions but prevent them from executing these actions.
<CodeView
  codeText={`<Button disabled>
  <Button.Label>Button</Button.Label>
</Button>`}

**Sizes**

Similar to input forms, buttons have three sizes: Small (28px), Medium (default - 36px) and Large (48px).
<CodeView codeText={sizesButton} />

### Widths

**Default**

Flexible with the label inside the button.
<CodeView codeText={widthDefault} />

**Min width**

The minimum width is 112px.
<CodeView
  codeText={`<Button width="min">
  <Button.Label>Ok</Button.Label>
</Button>`}/>

**Full width**

When a button’s width is set 100%, the button fully expands to the full width of its parent container.
<CodeView
  codeText={`<Button width="full">
  <Button.Label>Button</Button.Label>
</Button>`}

### Buttons with icons

**Text & icon**

A button that contains a label and an icon on the left or right of the label.
<CodeView
  codeText={`<Button>
  <Button.Icon><Icon name="refresh"/></Button.Icon>
  <Button.Label>Refresh</Button.Label>
</Button>`}

**Orther Brand**

***Microsoft***
<CodeView
  codeText={brandMicrosoft}

***Google***
<CodeView
  codeText={brandGoogle}

**Icon only**

A button that contains an icon only.
<CodeView
  codeText={`<Button onlyIcon>
  <Button.Icon><Icon name="refresh"/></Button.Icon>
</Button>`}

### Button Group

The Button Group component shares the same styles and state as normal Buttons.

<CodeView codeText={groupStylesButton} />

The Button Group component shares the same sizes as normal Buttons. However, buttons in one group must be the same size.

<CodeView codeText={groupSizesButton} />

<CodeView codeText={groupIconsButton} />

## Design Reference

Two or more primary buttons should not be placed next to each other. Different than a primary button, two or more secondary buttons can be used in one layout.

<div className="Grid u-marginBottomLarge">
  <div className="u-sizeFull md:u-size1of2">
    <div className="u-flex">
      <Button variant="secondary">Button</Button>
      <Button className="u-marginLeftExtraSmall">Button</Button>
    </div>
    <div className="u-borderBottom u-borderLarge u-borderPositive u-marginTopSmall" />
    <div className="u-textPositive">Do</div>
  </div>
  <div className="u-sizeFull md:u-size1of2">
    <div className="u-flex">
      <Button>Button</Button>
      <Button className="u-marginLeftExtraSmall">Button</Button>
    </div>
    <div className="u-borderBottom u-borderLarge u-borderNegative u-marginTopSmall" />
    <div className="u-textNegative">Don't</div>
  </div>
</div>

## API

<ComponentApi metadata={props.data.Button} />
<ComponentApi metadata={props.data.ButtonGroup} exportedBy={props.data.Button} />

export const query = graphql`
  query ButtonGroupQuery {
    Button: componentMetadata(displayName: { eq: "Button" }) {
      ...ComponentApi_metadata
    ButtonGroup: componentMetadata(displayName: { eq: "ButtonGroup" }) {
      ...ComponentApi_metadata

---

# Calendar

Source: https://github.com/tutoruniverse/ahaui/blob/main/apps/docs/src/pages/components/calendar.mdx

title: Calendar

import ComponentApi from 'src/components/ComponentApi';

# Calendar

## Normal

Base on [react-calendar][1], modified default style.

<CodeView codeText={`() => {
  const [currentDate, setDate] = useState(new Date());
  return (
    <Calendar value={currentDate} onChange={date => setDate(currentDate)} />
  );
};`}

### DatePicker

Base on [react-date-picker][2], modified default style.

<CodeView codeText={`() => {
  const [currentDate, setDate] = useState(new Date());
  return (
    <DatePicker value={currentDate} onChange={date => setDate(currentDate)} />
  );
};`}

### DateRangePicker

Base on [@wojtekmaj/react-daterange-picker][4], modified default style.

<CodeView codeText={`() => {
  const [startDate, setStartDate] = useState([new Date(),new Date()]);
  return (
    <DateRangePicker value={startDate} onChange={date => setStartDate(date)} />
  );
};`}

### TimePicker

Base on [react-time-picker][3], modified default style.

<CodeView codeText={`() => {
  const [time, setTime] = useState('10:00');
  return (
    <TimePicker value={time} onChange={time => setTime(time)} />
  );
};`}

## Design Reference

N/A

## API

<ComponentApi metadata={props.data.DatePicker} />
<ComponentApi metadata={props.data.DateRangePicker} />
<ComponentApi metadata={props.data.TimePicker} />

export const query = graphql`
  query CalendarQuery {
    DatePicker: componentMetadata(displayName: { eq: "DatePicker" }) {
      ...ComponentApi_metadata
    DateRangePicker: componentMetadata(displayName: { eq: "DateRangePicker" }) {
      ...ComponentApi_metadata
    TimePicker: componentMetadata(displayName: { eq: "TimePicker" }) {
      ...ComponentApi_metadata

[1]: https://www.npmjs.com/package/react-calendar
[2]: https://www.npmjs.com/package/react-date-picker
[3]: https://www.npmjs.com/package/react-time-picker
[4]: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@wojtekmaj/react-daterange-picker

# Card

Source: https://github.com/tutoruniverse/ahaui/blob/main/apps/docs/src/pages/components/card.mdx

title: Card

import ComponentApi from 'src/components/ComponentApi';

import defaultCard from 'src/examples/Card/default';
import imageCard from 'src/examples/Card/image';
import listCard from 'src/examples/Card/list';
import dropdownCard from 'src/examples/Card/dropdown';

# Card

## Introduction

Cards are used to apply a container around a related grouping of information. The card body accommodates any layout or design, as long as its a grouping of related information.

## Examples

### Default card

A card is made up of 2 sections, a header and a body.

The card header can have a title and actions. The title is located on the left, while the actions row is located on the right side of the card header. A small secondary button is used to display a single action, such as creating, editing, or deleting. If there are multiple actions, an action overflow menu would be used instead.

The header has limitations, but the body section can accommodate any layout of related information.

The card structure parts can be removed to prevent the part from displaying.

<CodeView codeText={defaultCard} />

<CodeView codeText={dropdownCard} />

### No padding image

<CodeView codeText={imageCard} />

### No header card
The card header can be removed to prevent the card header from displaying.In some cases, using text in the body part to create Card title.

Use `<Card.Body>` to pad content inside a `<Card>`.

<CodeView codeText={`<Card>
  <Card.Body>This is some text within a card body.</Card.Body>
</Card>`}/>

Alternatively, you can use this shorthand version for Cards with body only, and no other children

<CodeView codeText={'<Card body>This is some text within a card body.</Card>'} />

## Design Reference

Use the correct button size.Don’t use the medium or large button on Card.Header

<div className="Grid u-marginBottomLarge">
  <div className="u-sizeFull md:u-size1of2">
    <img
      className="u-maxWidthFull"
      src={require('src/assets/ref/card-structure-do.jpg')}
      srcSet={`${require('src/assets/ref/card-structure-do@2x.jpg')} 2x`}
      alt="Card Do"
    <div className="u-borderBottom u-borderLarge u-borderPositive u-marginTopSmall" />
    <div className="u-textPositive">Do</div>
  </div>
  <div className="u-sizeFull md:u-size1of2">
    <img
      className="u-maxWidthFull"
      src={require('src/assets/ref/card-structure-dont.jpg')}
      srcSet={`${require('src/assets/ref/card-structure-dont@2x.jpg')} 2x`}
      alt="Card Dont"
    <div className="u-borderBottom u-borderLarge u-borderNegative u-marginTopSmall" />
    <div className="u-textNegative">Don't</div>
  </div>
</div>

## API

<ComponentApi metadata={props.data.metadata} />

export const query = graphql`
  query CardQuery {
    metadata: componentMetadata(displayName: { eq: "Card" }) {
      ...ComponentApi_metadata

# Carousel

import ComponentApi from 'src/components/ComponentApi';

# Carousel

## Introduction

A carousel allows multiple pieces of content to be featured in a predefined amount of space. The pieces are horizontally scrollable. The component is based on [Slick Carousel][1].
<img
  className="u-maxWidthFull"
  src={require('src/assets/structure/stb_carousel-structure.jpg')}
  srcSet={`${require('src/assets/structure/stb_carousel-structure@2x.jpg')} 2x`}
  alt="Carousel structure"
<ol className="u-paddingLeftLarge u-textGray u-marginTopTiny">
  <li>
    Navigation buttons&nbsp;
    <i className="u-text200">- Used to navigate horizontally.</i>
  </li>
  <li>
    Indicator&nbsp;
    <i className="u-text200">- Used to indicate the currently visible contents as well as the invisible contents left.</i>
  </li>
  <li>
    Content&nbsp;
    <i className="u-text200">- Pieces of content.</i>
  </li>
</ol>

## Examples

### Default

<CodeView codeText={defaultCarousel} />

### Indicator Inside

In case the carousel is displaying only one piece of content in full width, the component’s indicator can be placed inside the content.

<CodeView codeText={dotInsideCarousel} />

## Design Reference

N/A

## API

<ComponentApi metadata={props.data.metadata} />

export const query = graphql`
  query CarouselQuery {
    metadata: componentMetadata(displayName: { eq: "Carousel" }) {
      ...ComponentApi_metadata

[1]: http://kenwheeler.github.io/slick/

# Chat Box

Source: https://github.com/tutoruniverse/ahaui/blob/main/apps/docs/src/pages/components/chat-box.mdx

title: Chat Box

import defaultChatBox from 'src/examples/ChatBox/default';
import fullWidthChatBox from 'src/examples/ChatBox/fullWidth';

# Chat Box

## Introduction

ChatBox is an interactive area which is designed to allow users to chat with each other through sending messages and attachments.

## Examples

Some examples of full components ChatBox.

### Default

Default ChatBox is designed for use on the left/right of the screen.

<CodeView codeText={defaultChatBox} />

### Full-width

ChatBox can be expanded to be a larger space in the design.

<CodeView codeText={fullWidthChatBox} />

## Design Reference

**(Ex:) Set max-width 560px for bubble chat in full-width ChatBox**

In order to ensure the user reading experience with the number of words on a line is not too large, the width of the bubble chat should be controlled in the case of the full-width ChatBox.

<div className="Grid u-marginBottomLarge">
  <div className="u-sizeFull md:u-size1of2">
    <img
      className="u-maxWidthFull"
      src={require('src/assets/ref/bubble-chat-structure-do.jpg')}
      srcSet={`${require('src/assets/ref/bubble-chat-structure-do@2x.jpg')} 2x`}
      alt="Accordion Do"
    <div className="u-borderBottom u-borderLarge u-borderPositive u-marginTopSmall" />
    <div className="u-textPositive">Do</div>
  </div>
  <div className="u-sizeFull md:u-size1of2">
    <img
      className="u-maxWidthFull"
      src={require('src/assets/ref/bubble-chat-structure-dont.jpg')}
      srcSet={`${require('src/assets/ref/bubble-chat-structure-dont@2x.jpg')} 2x`}
      alt="Accordion Dont"
    <div className="u-borderBottom u-borderLarge u-borderNegative u-marginTopSmall" />
    <div className="u-textNegative">Don't</div>
  </div>
</div>

    <i className="u-text200">
      - A button that lets users attach files.
    </i>
  </li>
  <li>
    Top divider
    <i className="u-text200">

    </i>
  </li>

# Dropdown

Source: https://github.com/tutoruniverse/ahaui/blob/main/apps/docs/src/pages/components/dropdown.mdx

title: Dropdown

import ComponentApi from 'src/components/ComponentApi';
import downLeft from 'src/examples/Dropdown/downLeft';
import downRight from 'src/examples/Dropdown/downRight';
import upLeft from 'src/examples/Dropdown/upLeft';
import upRight from 'src/examples/Dropdown/upRight';

# Dropdown

## Introduction

Dropdowns are contextual overlays used to display lists of actions, which are triggered by toggleable parent objects (i.e. buttons).
<img
  src={require('src/assets/structure/stb_dropdown-structure.jpg')}
  srcSet={`${require('src/assets/structure/stb_dropdown-structure@2x.jpg')} 2x`}
  className="u-maxWidthFull"
  alt="Dropdown"
<ol className="u-textGray u-marginTopTiny">
  <li>
    Menu
    <i className="u-text200"> - Contain actionable items.</i>
  </li>
  <li>
    Parent object
    <i className="u-text200"> - Toggleable objects that trigger the overlays. </i>
  </li>
</ol>

## Examples

### Directions

Based on the position of it’s parent object (i.e. buttons), the dropdowns will be displayed with several directions:

#### Down-left

<CodeView codeText={downLeft} />

#### Down-right

<CodeView codeText={downRight} />

#### Up-left

<CodeView codeText={upLeft} />

#### Up-right

<CodeView codeText={upRight} />

## Design Reference

N/A

## API

<ComponentApi metadata={props.data.Dropdown} />
<ComponentApi metadata={props.data.DropdownButton} exportedBy={props.data.Dropdown} />
<ComponentApi metadata={props.data.DropdownToggle} exportedBy={props.data.Dropdown} />
<ComponentApi metadata={props.data.DropdownContainer} exportedBy={props.data.Dropdown} />

export const query = graphql`
  query DropdownMDXQuery {
    Dropdown: componentMetadata(displayName: { eq: "Dropdown" }) {
      displayName
      ...ComponentApi_metadata
    DropdownButton: componentMetadata(displayName: { eq: "DropdownButton" }) {
      displayName
      ...ComponentApi_metadata
    DropdownToggle: componentMetadata(displayName: { eq: "DropdownToggle" }) {
      displayName
      ...ComponentApi_metadata
    DropdownContainer: componentMetadata(displayName: { eq: "DropdownContainer" }) {
      displayName
      ...ComponentApi_metadata

# Empty State

## Introduction

Empty states are moments in a user’s experience with a product where there is nothing to display.

<img
  src={require('src/assets/structure/stb_empty-states-structure.jpg')}
  srcSet={`${require('src/assets/structure/stb_empty-states-structure@2x.jpg')} 2x`}
  className="u-maxWidthFull"
  alt="Empty states"
<ol className="u-textGray u-marginTopTiny">
  <li>
    Illustration
    <i className="u-text200"> - It has a purpose to overview or add more detail for the title below.</i>
  </li>
  <li>
    Heading
    <i className="u-text200"> - Naming the state or call to action content.</i>
  </li>
  <li>
    Description
    <i className="u-text200"> - Adding more detail for the heading, giving directions for users to walk-through the empty states.</i>
  </li>
  <li>
    CTA Buttons
    <i className="u-text200"> - CTA Buttons - Optional call to actions to walk-through the empty states.</i>
  </li>
</ol>

## Examples

### General empty

Nothing to show.

<CodeView codeText={generalEmptyState} />

# File Attachment

## Introduction

The File Attachment component is using to show the attached file types which were browsed and chosen by users from the input file field.

<img
  src={require('src/assets/structure/stb_file-attachment-structure.jpg')}
  srcSet={`${require('src/assets/structure/stb_file-attachment-structure@2x.jpg')} 2x`}
  className="u-maxWidthFull"
  alt="File Attachment"
<ol className="u-textGray u-marginTopTiny">
  <li>
    File type icon
    <i className="u-text200"> - Showing an icon of text files, images, code files, etc.</i>
  </li>
  <li>
    File type label
    <i className="u-text200"> - In some cases, there are some file types that used the same icon. So this file type label can specifically show the file type. For example, .PNG and .JPG will be used as the same icon for images.</i>
  </li>
  <li>
    File name label
    <i className="u-text200"> -  Showing the name of the file.</i>
  </li>
  <li>
    Remove button
    <i className="u-text200"> - (Optional) Designed to remove the attached file purpose.</i>
  </li>
  <li>
    Actions
    <i className="u-text200"> - (Optional) Designed to show the actions when using the file attachment component as bubble chat.</i>
  </li>
  <li>
    Background
    <i className="u-text200"> - Including background-color and background-border, it helps to separate the file with each other.</i>
  </li>
</ol>

## Examples

### Text file

Using for .txt file.

<CodeView codeText={textFileAttachment} />

### Image file

Using for .png, .jpg and .gif files

<CodeView codeText={imageFileAttachment} />

### Code file

Using for .html, .svg, .js and .md files.

<CodeView codeText={codeFileAttachment} />

### Spreadsheet file

Using for .xlsx and .csv files.

<CodeView codeText={spreadsheetFileAttachment} />

### PowerPoint file

Using for .ppt and .pptx files.

<CodeView codeText={powerpointFileAttachment} />

### Query file

Using for .sql file.

<CodeView codeText={queryFileAttachment} />

### With actions

Users can click on the buttons to execute the corresponding features. The maximum of buttons is 2.

<CodeView codeText={withActionsFileAttachment} />

## Design Reference

N/A

## API

<ComponentApi metadata={props.data.metadata} />

  query FileAttachmentQuery {
    metadata: componentMetadata(displayName: { eq: "FileAttachment" }) {
      ...ComponentApi_metadata

# Checkbox and Radio Button

title: Form Check
import ComponentApi from 'src/components/ComponentApi';

import multipleRadioButtons from 'src/examples/Form/multipleRadioButtons';

# Checkbox and Radio Button

## Introduction
### Checkbox

A checkbox is a square box that is checked when activated. Checkboxes allow users to choose multiple options over a series of options.

<img
  className="u-maxWidthFull"
  src={require('src/assets/structure/stb_check-box-structure.jpg')}
  srcSet={`${require('src/assets/structure/stb_check-box-structure@2x.jpg')} 2x`}
  alt="Checkbox structure"
<ol className="u-paddingLeftLarge u-textGray u-marginTopTiny">
  <li>
      Checkbox icon  &nbsp;
    <i className="u-text200">- a 16x16px square box icon that indicates different states of a checkbox.</i>
  </li>
  <li>
      Label&nbsp;
    <i className="u-text200">- Standard label alignment is left-aligned and on the right of the checkbox icon.</i>
  </li>
</ol>

### Radio Button

A radio button is a small circle button that is checked when activated. Radio buttons allow users to choose only one option over a series of options.

<img
  className="u-maxWidthFull"
  src={require('src/assets/structure/stb_radio-button-structure.jpg')}
  srcSet={`${require('src/assets/structure/stb_radio-button-structure@2x.jpg')} 2x`}
  alt="Radio button structure"

<ol className="u-paddingLeftLarge u-textGray u-marginTopTiny ">
  <li>
      Radio button icon  &nbsp;
    <i className="u-text200">- a 16x16px circle box icon that indicates different states of a radio button.</i>
  </li>
  <li>
      Label&nbsp;
    <i className="u-text200">- Standard label alignment is left-aligned and on the right of the checkbox icon.</i>
  </li>
</ol>

## Examples

### Normal

<CodeView codeText={checkNormal}/>

### Disabled

<CodeView codeText={checkDisabled}/>

### Selected

<CodeView codeText={checkSelected}/>

### Selected Disabled

<CodeView codeText={checkSelectedDisabled}/>

### Valid/Invalid

<CodeView codeText={checkFeedback}/>

### Custom label

<CodeView codeText={checkCustomLabel}/>

### Button label

<CodeView codeText={checkButtonLabel}/>

### Multiple radio buttons

<CodeView codeText={multipleRadioButtons}/>

## Design Reference
N/A

## API

<ComponentApi metadata={props.data.FormCheck} exportedBy={props.data.Form} />

export const query = graphql`
  query FormCheckQuery {
    Form: componentMetadata(displayName: { eq: "Form" }) {
      ...ComponentApi_metadata
    FormCheck: componentMetadata(displayName: { eq: "FormCheck" }) {
      ...ComponentApi_metadata

# Inputs

## Introduction

Input fields/areas that allow users to enter/edit the input values.

### Text input (single line)

<img
  src={require('src/assets/structure/stb_input-text-field.jpg')}
  srcSet={`${require('src/assets/structure/stb_input-text-field@2x.jpg')} 2x`}
  className="u-maxWidthFull"
  alt="Input structure"

### Textarea (multiple lines)
<img
  src={require('src/assets/structure/stb_input-text-area.jpg')}
  srcSet={`${require('src/assets/structure/stb_input-text-area@2x.jpg')} 2x`}
  className="u-maxWidthFull"
  alt="Input structure"

<ol className="u-paddingLeftLarge u-textGray u-marginTopTiny">
  <li>
    Label  &nbsp;
    <i className="u-text200">- Short descriptive text which corresponds to the information required inside the field.</i>
  </li>
  <li>
    Placeholder&nbsp;
    <i className="u-text200">- The placeholder specifies a short hint that describes the expected value of an input field (i.e. a sample value or a short description of the expected format).</i>
  </li>
  <li>
    Value&nbsp;
    <i className="u-text200">- The value specifies the text information, data or value which is entered by users.</i>
  </li>
  <li>
    Feedback&nbsp;
    <i className="u-text200">- The feedback displays the messages from the system in specific cases i.e. invalid input, valid input, etc.</i>
  </li>
  <li>
    Input border&nbsp;
    <i className="u-text200">- The input border attribute specifies different input states (hovered, invalid, valid, etc.) by colors.</i>
  </li>
  <li>
    Input background&nbsp;
    <i className="u-text200">- The standard input background is white. It will only be changed to grey when the field is disabled.</i>
  </li>
</ol>

### States

**Normal**

**Disabled**

Disabled fields can’t be focused on. Their values are uneditable and can be passed through the submission process

<CodeView codeText={inputDisabled} />

**Read-only**

Read-only fields’ values are uneditable but can be focused and passed through the submission process

<CodeView codeText={inputReadOnly} />

**Valid**

Valid fields contain values which are verified by real-time checking system

<CodeView codeText={inputValid} />

**Invalid**

Invalid fields contain values which are marked as invalid by real-time checking system

<CodeView codeText={inputInvalid} />

## Form Group

Input group wraps inputs and buttons for more complex components.

Place one add-on or button on either side of an input. You may also place one on both sides of an input. Remember to place  `<label>` above the input group.

## Design Reference

Don’t use multiple lines for label & feedback

<div className="Grid u-marginBottomLarge">
  <div className="u-sizeFull md:u-size1of2">
    <Form.Group controlId="exampleForm.DSRe1">
      <Form.Label>Input</Form.Label>
      <Form.Input isValid type="text"></Form.Input>
      <Form.Feedback>Lorem Ipsum is simply dummy text</Form.Feedback>
    </Form.Group>
    <div className="u-borderBottom u-borderLarge u-borderPositive u-marginTopSmall u-paddingTopMedium" />
    <div className="u-textPositive">Do</div>
  </div>
  <div className="u-sizeFull md:u-size1of2">
    <Form.Group controlId="exampleForm.DSRe2">
      <Form.Label>Input</Form.Label>
      <Form.Input isInvalid type="text"></Form.Input>
      <Form.Feedback type="invalid">Lorem Ipsum is simply dummy text</Form.Feedback>
      <Form.Feedback type="invalid">Lorem Ipsum is simply dummy text</Form.Feedback>
    </Form.Group>
    <div className="u-borderBottom u-borderLarge u-borderNegative u-marginTopSmall" />
    <div className="u-textNegative">Don't</div>
  </div>
</div>

Avoid too long placeholder, label & feedback

<div className="Grid u-marginBottomLarge">
  <div className="u-sizeFull md:u-size1of2">
    <Form.Group controlId="exampleForm.DSRe3" className="u-paddingBottomTiny">
      <Form.Label>Input</Form.Label>
      <Form.Input isValid type="text" placeholder="Lorem Ipsum is simply dummy text"></Form.Input>
      <Form.Feedback>Lorem Ipsum is simply dummy text</Form.Feedback>
    </Form.Group>
    <div className="u-borderBottom u-borderLarge u-borderPositive u-marginTopSmall u-paddingTopSmall" />
    <div className="u-textPositive">Do</div>
  </div>
  <div className="u-sizeFull md:u-size1of2">
    <Form.Group controlId="exampleForm.DSRe4">
      <Form.Label>Input</Form.Label>
      <Form.Input isInvalid type="text" placeholder="Lorem Ipsum is simply dummy text of the printing and typesetting industry."></Form.Input>
      <Form.Feedback type="invalid">Lorem Ipsum is simply dummy text of the printing and typesetting industry. Lorem Ipsum has been the industry.</Form.Feedback>
    </Form.Group>
    <div className="u-borderBottom u-borderLarge u-borderNegative u-marginTopSmall" />
    <div className="u-textNegative">Don't</div>
  </div>
</div>

## API

<ComponentApi metadata={props.data.FormInput} exportedBy={props.data.Form} />
<ComponentApi metadata={props.data.FormFeedback} exportedBy={props.data.Form} />
<ComponentApi metadata={props.data.FormFile} exportedBy={props.data.Form} />

    Form: componentMetadata(displayName: { eq: "Form" }) {
      ...ComponentApi_metadata
    FormInput: componentMetadata(displayName: { eq: "FormInput" }) {
      ...ComponentApi_metadata
    FormFeedback: componentMetadata(displayName: { eq: "FormFeedback" }) {
      ...ComponentApi_metadata
    FormFile: componentMetadata(displayName: { eq: "FormFile" }) {
      ...ComponentApi_metadata
    FormGroup: componentMetadata(displayName: { eq: "FormGroup" }) {
      ...ComponentApi_metadata
    FormLabel: componentMetadata(displayName: { eq: "FormLabel" }) {
      ...ComponentApi_metadata
    FormSelect: componentMetadata(displayName: { eq: "FormSelect" }) {
      ...ComponentApi_metadata
    FormGroup: componentMetadata(displayName: { eq: "FormGroup" }) {
      ...ComponentApi_metadata

# Header

## Introduction

Header structure is a template that explains the areas in the header and how it work which helps combine other components to create a consistent user experience.

### Default

<img
  src={require('src/assets/structure/default-header-structure.jpg')}
  srcSet={`${require('src/assets/structure/default-header-structure@2x.jpg')} 2x`}
  alt="Header structure"
  className="u-maxWidthFull"
<ol className="u-textGray u-marginTopTiny">
  <li>Container: Using container to wrap header contents and grid system to set fix-width or full-width header.</li>
  <li>Logo: Using this area for logo of the site.</li>
  <li>Main content wrapper: Used to wrap all the header contents, except logo. This part is also replaced by a hamburger button on mobile.</li>
  <li>Right: Often used to present icons, CTA buttons or components about users' account.</li>
  <li>Left: Often used to display top menu of the site.</li>
</ol>

### Absolute

<img
  src={require('src/assets/structure/absolute-header-structure.jpg')}
  srcSet={`${require('src/assets/structure/absolute-header-structure@2x.jpg')} 2x`}
  alt="Header structure"
  className="u-maxWidthFull"
<ol className="u-textGray u-marginTopTiny">
  <li>Container: Using container to wrap header contents and grid system to set fix-width or full-width header.</li>
  <li>Logo: Using this area for logo of the site.</li>
  <li>Main content wrapper: Used to wrap all the header contents, except logo. This part is also replaced by a hamburger button on mobile.</li>
  <li>Right: Often used to present icons, CTA buttons or components about users' account.</li>
  <li>Absolute center-aligned objects: Using this area to display the components which are always center-aligned such as a countdown or session remaining component in workspace.</li>
</ol>

## Examples

### Desktop layout

Note: Only "LEFT" area or "CENTER" area is shown up at a time.

### Examples

# Icons

Source: https://github.com/tutoruniverse/ahaui/blob/main/apps/docs/src/pages/components/icon.mdx

title: Icon
import { useState } from 'react';
import classNames from 'classnames';
import copy from 'copy-text-to-clipboard';
import { Icon, Form, Overlay, Tooltip } from '@ahaui/react';
import { icons } from '@ahaui/react/constants/icons';
import ComponentApi from 'src/components/ComponentApi';
import colorIcon from 'src/examples/Icon/color';
import sizeIcon from 'src/examples/Icon/size';

export const AllIcons = () => {
  const [iconDisplay, setIconDisplay] = useState(null);
  const [searchText, setSearchText] = useState("");
  const handleSearch = (e) => {
    const value = e.target.value;
    setIconDisplay(null);
    setSearchText(value.toLowerCase())
  return (
    <>
      <Form.Group controlId="search-icon" sizeControl="small">
        <Form.Input
          value={searchText}
          onChange={handleSearch}
          placeholder="Search icon ..."
      </Form.Group>
     {iconDisplay && (
        <CodeView horizontal show codeText={`<Icon size="medium" name="${iconDisplay}"/>`} />
      )}
      <div className="u-positionRelative u-paddingSmall u-marginBottomExtraSmall u-border u-borderSmall u-borderUltraLight u-roundedMedium">
        {Object.keys(icons).filter(item => item.includes(searchText)).map(item => (
          <div
            onClick={() => setIconDisplay(item)}
            key={item}
            className={classNames(
              'u-marginRightSmall u-marginBottomSmall u-cursorPointer u-inlineBlock',
              (iconDisplay === item) && 'u-textPrimary'
            )}
          >
          <Overlay.Trigger
            placement="bottom"
            delay={{ show: 500, hide: 1000 }}
            hoverOverlay
            overlay={props => (
              <Tooltip id="tooltip-icon-search" {...props}>
                  {item}
              </Tooltip>
            )}
            >
              <Icon name={item} size="medium" />
            </Overlay.Trigger>
          </div>
        ))}
      </div>
    </>
  )

# Icons

## Introduction

Icons are used to visualize the common actions, provide visual context and enhance usability. They should be simple, yet bold enough to grab users' attention.

### Icon grid

Regular icons are designed on an 18px grid and exported on a 24px artboard.

  alt="Icon grid"
<ol className="u-paddingLeftLarge u-textGray u-marginTopTiny">

    Container&nbsp;
    <i className="u-text200">- The exported icon canvas.</i>
  </li>
  <li>
    Padding&nbsp;
    <i className="u-text200">The white space around the actual icon.</i>
  </li>
  <li>
    Safe area&nbsp;
    <i className="u-text200">The area which is used to display the actual icon.</i>
  </li>
</ol>

### Shapes

# Media

Source: https://github.com/tutoruniverse/ahaui/blob/main/apps/docs/src/pages/components/media.mdx

title: Media

import ComponentApi from 'src/components/ComponentApi';

# Media

## Introduction

Allow browsers to determine video or slideshow dimensions based on the width of their containing block by creating an intrinsic ratio that will properly scale on any device.

You don't need to include `frameborder="0"`  in your iframes. The aspect ratio is controlled via the `aspectRatio` prop.

## Examples

### Element Type

<div className="Grid">
  <div className="u-sizeFull lg:u-size1of2 u-marginBottomMedium">
    <p>
      HTML5 Video Player by using&nbsp;
      <code>&lt;embed&gt;</code>
      &nbsp;tag:
    </p>
    <CodeView codeText={'<Media src="https://commondatastorage.googleapis.com/gtv-videos-bucket/sample/BigBuckBunny.mp4" type="video/webm" title="Video example" />'} />
  </div>
  <div className="u-sizeFull lg:u-size1of2 u-marginBottomMedium">
    <p>
      Showing an image by using&nbsp;
      <code>&lt;img&gt;</code>
      &nbsp;tag:
    </p>
    <CodeView codeText={'<Media as="img" src="https://images.pexels.com/photos/461198/pexels-photo-461198.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&dpr=3&h=750&w=1260" alt="Image" title="Image from https://images.pexels.com" />'} />
  </div>
</div>

### Aspect Ratio

Embed Google Maps and videos from Youtube, Vimeo by using `<iframe>` tag:

<div className="Grid">
  <div className="u-sizeFull lg:u-size1of2 u-marginBottomMedium">
    <p><em>Square (1:1)</em></p>
    <CodeView codeText={'<Media as="iframe" aspectRatio="square" src="https://www.google.com/maps/embed?pb=!1m18!1m12!1m3!1d50585.80752281471!2d-122.40243146636166!3d37.58773037709596!2m3!1f0!2f0!3f0!3m2!1i1024!2i768!4f13.1!3m3!1m2!1s0x808f7625549b8e59%3A0xbbcfa3e532f8f4f!2sBurlingame%2C%20CA%2C%20USA!5e0!3m2!1sen!2s!4v1587037928284!5m2!1sen!2s" />'} />
  </div>
  <div className="u-sizeFull lg:u-size1of2 u-marginBottomMedium">
    <p><em>Classic (4:3)</em></p>
    <CodeView codeText={'  <Media as="iframe" aspectRatio="classic" src="https://www.google.com/maps/embed?pb=!1m18!1m12!1m3!1d50585.80752281471!2d-122.40243146636166!3d37.58773037709596!2m3!1f0!2f0!3f0!3m2!1i1024!2i768!4f13.1!3m3!1m2!1s0x808f7625549b8e59%3A0xbbcfa3e532f8f4f!2sBurlingame%2C%20CA%2C%20USA!5e0!3m2!1sen!2s!4v1587037928284!5m2!1sen!2s" />'} />
  </div>
  <div className="u-sizeFull lg:u-size1of2 u-marginBottomMedium">
    <p><em>Wide (16:9)</em></p>
    <CodeView codeText={'<Media as="iframe" aspectRatio="wide" src="https://player.vimeo.com/video/311342841?title=0&byline=0&portrait=0" />'} />
  </div>
  <div className="u-sizeFull lg:u-size1of2 u-marginBottomMedium">
    <p><em>Cinema (21:9)</em></p>
    <CodeView codeText={' <Media as="iframe" aspectRatio="cinema" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/ISJMsVhY5Yk" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture" />'} />
  </div>
</div>

# Message

## Introduction

Using messages to communicate between system and users, to notify or to show the system's responses to user’s actions.

<img
  src={require('src/assets/structure/stb_message-structure.jpg')}
  srcSet={`${require('src/assets/structure/stb_message-structure@2x.jpg')} 2x`}
  alt="Message structure"
<ol className="u-textGray u-marginTopTiny">
  <li>
        Heading
    <i className="u-text200"> -  Like a message title, using heading for message overview purpose.</i>
  </li>
  <li>
        Message
    <i className="u-text200"> -  The information that the system wants to send to users. Message content can include paragraphs and links.</i>
  </li>
  <li>
        Close button
    <i className="u-text200"> - Optional to close the message immediately.</i>
  </li>
  <li>
        CTA button
    <i className="u-text200"> -  Designed for system messages only. CTA button is the main action that users can interact with a system message.</i>
  </li>
  <li>
        Background
    <i className="u-text200"> - The message background attribute specifies the message variants by color changing.</i>
  </li>
</ol>

## Examples

### Types

#### Form messages

Form messages are alerts that provide contextual feedback messages for user actions with input forms. It's available for any length of text, as well as an optional dismiss button.

<CodeView codeText={formMessage} />

#### System messages

System messages provide contextual feedback messages for typical user actions with the handful of available and flexible alert messages. It's available for any length of text, a CTA button, as well as an optional dismiss button.

<CodeView codeText={systemMessage} />

### Variants

#### Form messages

<CodeView exampleClassName="example-messages" codeText={variantFormMessage} />

#### System messages

<CodeView exampleClassName="example-messages" codeText={variantSystemMessage} />

### Layout

<CodeView codeText={layoutMessage} />
<CodeView codeText={layout2Message} />
<CodeView codeText={layout3Message} />
<CodeView codeText={layout4Message} />
<CodeView codeText={layout5Message} />

      ...ComponentApi_metadata

title: Modal
import ComponentApi from 'src/components/ComponentApi';

import smallModal from 'src/examples/Modal/small';

import stepModal from 'src/examples/Modal/step';
import launchModal from 'src/examples/Modal/launch';
import askModal from 'src/examples/Modal/ask';

# Modal

## Introduction

Using modals to provide an opportunity to display content in a layer above the app, requiring user interaction with focused actions or alerts.

Standard modals are basic containers with a close `“X”`. The primary action button is a primary system color, other actions are secondary color.

<img
  src={require('src/assets/structure/stb_modal-structure.jpg')}
  srcSet={`${require('src/assets/structure/stb_modal-structure@2x.jpg')} 2x`}
  alt="Modal structure"
<ol className="u-textGray u-marginTopTiny">
  <li>
      Header
    <i className="u-text200"> -  Contains modal title and close button.</i>
  </li>
  <li>
      Body
    <i className="u-text200"> - Includes paragraphs, forms, images or icons which have a purpose to overview or add more detail for the modal title, or provide input forms to get data from users to complete a task. The body has top padding is 16px while left, right and bottom padding are 24px.</i>
  </li>
  <li>
      Footer
    <i className="u-text200"> - Contains CTA buttons and notes for the actions.</i>
  </li>
  <li>
      Container
    <i className="u-text200"> - Using container as a wrapper of header, body, and footer; make a separation between modal and the background by its shadow.</i>
  </li>
</ol>

## Examples

### Sizes

Depends on content to choose a suitable modal size.

#### Small

<CodeView exampleClassName="example-modal" codeText={smallModal} />

#### Medium

<CodeView exampleClassName="example-modal" codeText={mediumModal} />

#### Large

<CodeView exampleClassName="example-modal" codeText={largeModal} />

#### Extra large

<CodeView exampleClassName="example-modal" codeText={extraLargeModal} />

### Footer types

#### One CTA

Using a full width button for CTA to gain more focus and expand the click area.

<CodeView exampleClassName="example-modal" codeText={oneCTAModal} />

#### Two CTA

Using auto-width buttons for CTAs and left-aligned as default.

<CodeView exampleClassName="example-modal" codeText={twoCTAModal} />

#### Two CTA - Full width

Using 2 full width buttons in some case CTA button's copies are too long.

<CodeView exampleClassName="example-modal" codeText={twoCTAFullModal} />

#### Two CTA - 2 columns

Using 2 columns button for small modal size only to keep balance.

<CodeView exampleClassName="example-modal" codeText={twoCTAPartModal} />

#### Multiple steps

Using for showing multiple steps of modals. A primary button is right-aligned for next action and a secondary button is left-aligned for back action.

<CodeView exampleClassName="exampleModal" codeText={stepModal} />

#### Accent buttons

Replace a primary button by an accent button when using modal for Ask flow or Payment flow with all types.

<CodeView exampleClassName="example-modal" codeText={askModal} />

### Live demo

<CodeView codeText={launchModal} />

# Overlay

Source: https://github.com/tutoruniverse/ahaui/blob/main/apps/docs/src/pages/components/overlay.mdx

title: Overlay

import ComponentApi from 'src/components/ComponentApi';

import basicOverlay from 'src/examples/Overlay/default';
import triggerOverlay from 'src/examples/Overlay/trigger';
import shortTooltip from 'src/examples/Overlay/tooltip';
import shortTooltipWhite from 'src/examples/Overlay/tooltipWhite';
import longTooltip from 'src/examples/Overlay/tooltipLong';
import basicDelay from 'src/examples/Overlay/basicDelay';
import delayWithHoverOverlay from 'src/examples/Overlay/delayWithHoverOverlay';

# Overlay

## Introduction

A set of components for positioning beautiful overlays, tooltips, and anything else you need.

### Overlay

`Overlay` is the fundamental component for positioning and controlling tooltip visibility. It's a wrapper around react-popper, that adds support for transitions, and visibility toggling.

### Overlay trigger

Since the above pattern is pretty common, but verbose, we've included `<Overlay.Trigger>`  component to help with common use-cases. It even has functionality to delayed show or hides, and a few different "trigger" events you can mix and match.

### Tooltips

Tooltips provide a small amount of information to an element on hover. Typically, tooltips are used to help users understand the meaning or purpose of icons, showing the full version of truncated text.

<img
  src={require('src/assets/structure/stb_tooltips-structure.jpg')}
  srcSet={`${require('src/assets/structure/stb_tooltips-structure@2x.jpg')} 2x`}
  className="u-maxWidthFull"
  alt="Tooltip"
<ol className="u-textGray u-marginTopTiny">
  <li>
          Label
    <i className="u-text200"> - Showing the information which makes more sense for an element.</i>
  </li>
  <li>
          Background
    <i className="u-text200"> - Default is transparent black background.</i>
  </li>
  <li>
          Arrow
    <i className="u-text200"> - Depending on the direction of the tooltips to set a small arrow's position which can be on top, bottom, left of right.</i>
  </li>
</ol>

## Examples

### Basic

You can pass the `Overlay`  injected props directly to the `Tooltip` component.

<CodeView codeText={basicOverlay} />

Or pass a `Tooltip` component to  `Overlay.Trigger` instead.

<CodeView codeText={triggerOverlay} />

### Tooltip placement

Short content.

<CodeView codeText={shortTooltip} />

Long content.

<CodeView codeText={longTooltip} />

### White

<CodeView codeText={shortTooltipWhite} />

### Delay

Basic delay.

<CodeView codeText={basicDelay} />

If your want the tooltip not to disappear when you hover it, combine `delay` and `hoverOverlay`.

<CodeView codeText={delayWithHoverOverlay} />

## Design Reference

N/A

## API

<ComponentApi metadata={props.data.Overlay} />
<ComponentApi metadata={props.data.OverlayTrigger} exportedBy={props.data.Overlay} />
<ComponentApi metadata={props.data.Tooltip} />

export const query = graphql`
  query OverlayQuery {
    Tooltip: componentMetadata(displayName: { eq: "Tooltip" }) {
      ...ComponentApi_metadata
    Overlay: componentMetadata(displayName: { eq: "Overlay" }) {
      ...ComponentApi_metadata
    OverlayTrigger: componentMetadata(displayName: { eq: "OverlayTrigger" }) {
      ...ComponentApi_metadata

---

# Pagination

Source: https://github.com/tutoruniverse/ahaui/blob/main/apps/docs/src/pages/components/pagination.mdx

title: Pagination

import ComponentApi from 'src/components/ComponentApi';

import centerAlignedPagination from 'src/examples/Pagination/centerAligned';
import leftAlignedPagination from 'src/examples/Pagination/leftAligned';
import sizesPagination from 'src/examples/Pagination/sizes';
import lessThan7Pagination from 'src/examples/Pagination/lessThan7';
import moreThan7Pagination from 'src/examples/Pagination/moreThan7';

# Pagination

## Introduction

Using pagination to navigate pages of component listings. It helps users easily move between a large number of pages.

<img
  src={require('src/assets/structure/stb_pagination-structure.jpg')}
  srcSet={`${require('src/assets/structure/stb_pagination-structure@2x.jpg')} 2x`}
  alt="Pagination structure"
<ol className="u-textGray u-marginTopTiny">
  <li>
    Previous/Next
    <i className="u-text200"> - Navigate backward and forwards from the currently selected page.</i>
  </li>
  <li>
    Page navigation
    <i className="u-text200"> - Navigate to a specific page by selecting the page number.</i>
  </li>
  <li>
    Truncation
    <i className="u-text200"> - When a threshold of pages is reached, the list is truncated using ellipses.</i>
  </li>
</ol>

## Examples

The Previous button, Next button, First-page item, and Last-page item are always visible by default. The UI could be different depends on the number of pages.

### Alignment

#### Center

<CodeView codeText={centerAlignedPagination} />

#### Left

<CodeView codeText={leftAlignedPagination} />

### Sizes

Pagination component shares the same sizes as the Buttons component. However, buttons in pagination must be the same size.

<CodeView exampleClassName="example-paginations" codeText={sizesPagination} />

### Structure

#### Less than or equal to 7 items

If the first page is active, then the Previous button will be disabled. If the last page is active, then the Next button will be disabled.

<CodeView exampleClassName="example-paginations" codeText={lessThan7Pagination} />

#### More than 7 items

Except for the Previous and Next buttons, the total number of visible items is fixed to 7. While the first and last items are always visible, 5 extant items can move around.

<CodeView exampleClassName="example-paginations" codeText={moreThan7Pagination} />

## Design Reference

N/A

## API

<ComponentApi metadata={props.data.Pagination} />
<ComponentApi metadata={props.data.PaginationItem} exportedBy={props.data.Pagination} />

export const query = graphql`
  query PaginationMDXQuery {
    Pagination: componentMetadata(displayName: { eq: "Pagination" }) {
      ...ComponentApi_metadata
    PaginationItem: componentMetadata(displayName: { eq: "PaginationItem" }) {
      ...ComponentApi_metadata

---

# Progress

## Introduction

The component is used to help users to indicate the current state; and guide them through a set of steps in a specific process.

    <i className="u-text200"> - An animated or fixed bar which is used to indicate the current state of the process.</i>
  </li>
  <li>
      Label
    <i className="u-text200"> - A text object, which is used to shortly describe the current state (i.e. percentage).</i>
  </li>
  <li>
      Progress bar
    <i className="u-text200">
        - A fixed-width bar, with outlined or secondary colors, that indicates the whole process.
    </i>
  </li>

</ol>

# Sidebar Menu

title: Sidebar Menu

import ComponentApi from 'src/components/ComponentApi';

# Sidebar Menu

## Introduction

Sidebar is a graphical control element that displays main navigation to the right or left side of an application window or operating system desktop to navigate away between pages.

<img
  src={require('src/assets/structure/stb_sidebar-structure.jpg')}
  srcSet={`${require('src/assets/structure/stb_sidebar-structure@2x.jpg')} 2x`}
  className="u-maxWidthFull"
  alt="Sidebar"
<ol className="u-textGray u-marginTopTiny">
  <li>
      Left icon
    <i className="u-text200"> - Used to visualize the Menu Item and provide visual context and enhance usability. Menu Items in sub-menus do not support the left icon. Left icons are optional.</i>
  </li>
  <li>
      Label
    <i className="u-text200"> - Concise & descriptive title of the content within.</i>
  </li>
  <li>
      Badge
    <i className="u-text200"> - An optional right-aligned badge, that contains a status or a numeric value, to indicate a running tally or a quantity-based summary.</i>
  </li>
  <li>
      Toggle icon
    <i className="u-text200"> - A left-aligned icon, used to visualize the sub-menu and provide clickable action to open and close the sub-menu.</i>
  </li>
  <li>
      Indicator
    <i className="u-text200"> - A left border which indicates active items.</i>
  </li>
  <li>
      Background
    <i className="u-text200"> - A slight change in background color of the item when hovered or selected.</i>
  </li>
</ol>

## Examples

### Levels

### Sizes

#### Medium

Default size.

<CodeView codeText={sizeMediumSidebarMenu} transparentBackground />

#### Small

<CodeView codeText={sizeSmallSidebarMenu} transparentBackground />

Smaller size can be applied for both Sidebar menu levels.

### States

#### Normal

Default state.

#### Active

Item background color will be changed to grey with the Indicator activated in primary color.

#### Disabled

Item background color will be changed to grey with the Indicator activated in primary color.

<CodeView codeText={statesSidebarMenu} />

# Skeleton

Source: https://github.com/tutoruniverse/ahaui/blob/main/apps/docs/src/pages/components/skeleton.mdx

title: Skeleton
import { Media, Icon, Skeleton, Avatar } from '@ahaui/react';
import ComponentApi from 'src/components/ComponentApi';

# Skeleton

## Introduction

Display a placeholder preview of the content before the data gets loaded to reduce load-time frustration. The Skeleton can be used to illustrate the layout of a component or block content.

By default, a single Skeleton item is basically a gray block of which the width and the height are set to 100% and 16px respectively.

## Examples

### Text

The default shape of the Skeleton and can be used to illustrate a text line. Two or more shapes can be used to represent a paragraph.

<CodeView codeText={'<Skeleton />'} />

### Circle

Often used to illustrate an Avatar.

<CodeView codeText={'<Skeleton variant="circle" width={40} height={40} />'} />

### Rectangle

To represent the media content such as image and video.

<CodeView codeText={'<Skeleton height={118} />'} />

### Other Examples

**Excelchat Learning Lesson Item**

<div className="u-flex u-paddingSmall u-border u-borderLighter u-roundedMedium u-marginBottomMedium">
  <div className="u-flex u-flexColumn u-flexShrink0  u-backgroundLightest" style={{ width: 210 }}>
    <Media src="https://s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/gotit-pro-prod-excel-private/learning/assets/module-thumbnails/thumbnail-module-1.png" />
    <div className="u-fontMedium u-paddingExtraSmall">Lesson 1</div>
  </div>
  <div className="u-marginLeftSmall u-flexGrow1">
    <div className="u-flex u-justifyContentBetween u-marginBottomSmall">
      <div className="u-text400 u-fontMedium u-flexGrow1">Spreadsheet Design</div>
      <div className="u-textGray u-text200 u-flex u-alignItemsCenter">
        <Icon name="timer" size="extraSmall" className="u-marginRightTiny" />
                  20 mins to complete
      </div>
    </div>
    <div className="u-textTruncate-3">Build your beautifully organized spreadsheet from scratch. In this Learning Module, you'll learn the essentials of formatting cells containing Text, Currency, Dates, and Numbers.</div>
  </div>
</div>
<CodeView codeText={`<div className="u-flex">
    <Skeleton width={210} height={118} />
    <div className="u-marginLeftSmall u-flexGrow1">
      <Skeleton width="60%" />
      <Skeleton />
      <Skeleton />
    </div>
</div>`}

**Table example**

<CodeView codeText={`<table className="Table u-backgroundWhite u-textDark u-text200">
      <thead>
        <tr>
          <th><Skeleton width="25%" /></th>
          <th><Skeleton width="25%" /></th>
          <th><Skeleton width="25%" /></th>
        </tr>
      </thead>
      <tbody>
        <tr>
          <td><Skeleton width="50%"/></td>
          <td><Skeleton width="50%"/></td>
          <td><Skeleton width="50%"/></td>
        </tr>
        <tr>
          <td><Skeleton /></td>
          <td><Skeleton /></td>
          <td><Skeleton /></td>
        </tr>
      </tbody>
    </table>`}

## Design Reference

**Use the correct shapes**

An avatar is always a circle even though it’s a photo, so don't use a rectangle or a square to represent an avatar.

<div className="Grid u-marginBottomLarge">
  <div className="u-sizeFull md:u-size1of4">
    <div>
      <div className="u-marginBottomSmall">
        <Avatar src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gotitinc/aha-assets/master/gotit/avatar/default.svg" width={96} height={96} />
      </div>
      <div className="u-fontMedium u-text400">Lucifer S.Morningstar </div>
      <div>Head of Design</div>
      <div>Got It, Inc.</div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div className="u-sizeFull md:u-size1of4 md:u-offset1of12">
    <div className="u-marginBottomSmall">
      <Skeleton variant="circle" width={96} height={96} />
    </div>
    <Skeleton width="50%" />
    <Skeleton width="50%" />
    <Skeleton width="25%" />
    <div className="u-borderBottom u-borderLarge u-borderPositive u-marginTopSmall" />
    <div className="u-textPositive">Do</div>
  </div>
  <div className="u-sizeFull md:u-size1of4 md:u-offset1of12">
    <div className="u-marginBottomSmall">
      <Skeleton width={96} height={96} />
    </div>
    <Skeleton width="50%" />
    <Skeleton width="50%" />
    <Skeleton width="25%" />
    <div className="u-borderBottom u-borderLarge u-borderNegative u-marginTopSmall" />
    <div className="u-textNegative">Don't</div>
  </div>
</div>

## API

<ComponentApi metadata={props.data.metadata} />

  query SkeletonQuery {
    metadata: componentMetadata(displayName: { eq: "Skeleton" }) {
      displayName
      ...ComponentApi_metadata

# Tab

<img
  src={require('src/assets/structure/stb_tabs-structure.jpg')}

import ComponentApi from 'src/components/ComponentApi';

# Tag Input

## Introduction

Tag input component allows users enter one or several tags to an input field.

This component is based on [react-tagsinput][1]

<img
  src={require('src/assets/structure/stb_tag-input-structure.jpg')}
  srcSet={`${require('src/assets/structure/stb_tag-input-structure@2x.jpg')} 2x`}
  className="u-maxWidthFull"
  alt="Tag Input"
<ol className="u-textGray u-marginTopTiny">
  <li>
    Tag-Input field
    <i className="u-text200"> - Be set single line as default, but it can be expand to several lines when users input more tags.</i>
  </li>
  <li>
    Placeholder
    <i className="u-text200"> - The placeholder attribute specifies a short hint that describes the expected value of an input field (e.g. Add a tag). The short hint is displayed in the input field before users typing a value and comebacks when a tag was selected.</i>
  </li>
  <li>
    Tags
    <i className="u-text200"> - The main values of the field, with removable tags allow users to remove.</i>
  </li>
  <li>
    Button
    <i className="u-text200"> - A button is separated from the field as default. In some cases, the button can be put next to the field, on the right side, as the form group.</i>
  </li>
</ol>

## Examples

### Variants

The value `primary_subtle` is used as the default style, but there are also many other styles to use.

<CodeView codeText={defaultTagInput} />
<CodeView codeText={variant1TagInput} />
<CodeView codeText={variant2TagInput} />

### With button

<CodeView codeText={widthButtonTagInput} />
<CodeView codeText={widthButton2TagInput} />

## Design Reference

N/A

## API

<ComponentApi metadata={props.data.metadata} />

[1]: https://www.npmjs.com/package/react-tagsinput
export const query = graphql`
  query TagInputQuery {
    metadata: componentMetadata(displayName: { eq: "TagInput" }) {
      ...ComponentApi_metadata

# Tag

Source: https://github.com/tutoruniverse/ahaui/blob/main/apps/docs/src/pages/components/tag.mdx

title: Tag
import { Tag } from '@ahaui/react';
import ComponentApi from 'src/components/ComponentApi';
import tagRemove from 'src/examples/Tag/remove';
import tagSubtle from 'src/examples/Tag/subtle';
import tagBold from 'src/examples/Tag/bold';

# Tag

## Introduction

Tags are used to label different objects, normally multiple objects with similar types, in a compact format. Tags are either removable or non-removable.

<img
  className="u-maxWidthFull"
  src={require('src/assets/structure/stb_tag-structure.jpg')}
  srcSet={`${require('src/assets/structure/stb_tag-structure@2x.jpg')} 2x`}
  alt="Tag structure"
<ol className="u-textGray u-marginTopTiny">
  <li>
    Background
  </li>
  <li>
    Text
  </li>
  <li>
    Icon&nbsp;
    <i className="u-text200">- Close button optional</i>
  </li>
</ol>

## Examples

### Tag text

<CodeView codeText={'<Tag>Default</Tag>'} />

### Removable tag

<CodeView codeText={tagRemove} />

### Subtle Style

Designed with light colors, subtle badges are used for less important information.

<CodeView codeText={tagSubtle} transparentBackground />

### Bold Style

Designed with bold colors, bold badges are used for important information.

<CodeView codeText={tagBold} />

## Design Reference

Don’t use multiple lines for label & feedback

<div className="Grid u-marginBottomLarge">
  <div className="u-sizeFull md:u-size1of2">
    <Tag>Tag</Tag>
    <div className="u-borderBottom u-borderLarge u-borderPositive u-marginTopSmall u-paddingTopSmall " />
    <div className="u-textPositive">Do</div>
  </div>
  <div className="u-sizeFull md:u-size1of2">
    <Tag>
      Tag
      <br />
      multiple lines
    </Tag>
    <div className="u-borderBottom u-borderLarge u-borderNegative u-marginTopSmall" />
    <div className="u-textNegative">Don't</div>
  </div>
</div>

## API

<ComponentApi metadata={props.data.metadata} />

export const query = graphql`
  query TagQuery {
    metadata: componentMetadata(displayName: { eq: "Tag" }) {
      displayName
      ...ComponentApi_metadata

# Toast Messages

Source: https://github.com/tutoruniverse/ahaui/blob/main/apps/docs/src/pages/components/toast.mdx

title: Toast

import ComponentApi from 'src/components/ComponentApi';

import defaultToast from 'src/examples/Toast/default';

# Toast Messages

## Introduction

It is a small message that shows up in a box at the corner of the screen and disappears on its own after a few seconds. It is simple feedback about an operation in which current activity remains visible and interactive.

<img
  src={require('src/assets/structure/stb_toast-messages-structure.jpg')}
  srcSet={`${require('src/assets/structure/stb_toast-messages-structure@2x.jpg')} 2x`}
  className="u-maxWidthFull"
  alt="Toast Messages"
<ol className="u-textGray u-marginTopTiny">
  <li>
  Heading
    <i className="u-text200">
- A title to explain what the message content is about.
    </i>
  </li>
  <li>
  Message
    <i className="u-text200"> - The information that the system wants to send to users. Message content can include paragraphs and links.</i>
  </li>
  <li>
  Close button
    <i className="u-text200"> - Optional to close the message immediately.</i>
  </li>
  <li>
  Progress bar
    <i className="u-text200"> - The display time remaining of the message before it disappears.</i>
  </li>
</ol>

## Examples

<CodeView codeText={defaultToast}/>

      ...ComponentApi_metadata

# Toggle

## Introduction

Toggles are normally used to switch between two states of a setting.

<img
  src={require('src/assets/structure/stb_toggles-structure.jpg')}
  srcSet={`${require('src/assets/structure/stb_toggles-structure@2x.jpg')} 2x`}

    Toggle button
    <span className="u-marginLeftTiny u-textNegative u-text200">(required)</span>
    &nbsp;
    <i className="u-text200">- Main component for users to interact with, including a thumb and a track.</i>
  </li>
  <li>
    Label
    <span className="u-marginLeftTiny u-text200">(optional)</span>
    &nbsp;
    <i className="u-text200">
      -  Standard label alignment is left-aligned and on the right of the toggle button.
    </i>
  </li>
</ol>

## Examples

### Disabled

# Top Banner

Source: https://github.com/tutoruniverse/ahaui/blob/main/apps/docs/src/pages/components/top-banner.mdx

title: Top Banner

import ComponentApi from 'src/components/ComponentApi';

# Top Banner

## Introduction

Top banner is a top section on the website, which is designed for promotional purposes.

<img
  src={require('src/assets/structure/stb_top-banner-structure.jpg')}
  srcSet={`${require('src/assets/structure/stb_top-banner-structure@2x.jpg')} 2x`}
  alt="Top banner structure"
<ol className="u-textGray u-marginTopTiny">
  <li>
    Message
    <i className="u-text200"> - A short (normally 1 line) text content.</i>
  </li>
  <li>
    Action
    <i className="u-text200"> - Resembles a button with an icon.</i>
  </li>
  <li>
    Close button
    <i className="u-text200"> - A button to close the banner (optional).</i>
  </li>
  <li>
    Background
    <i className="u-text200"> - An image or a color-background with the height of 48px.</i>
  </li>
</ol>

## Examples

### Styles

Depending on the promotion themes, the top banner will be designed flexibly by color scheme which was defined in the Color library.

* The height is fixed on all platforms (desktop, tablet and mobile).
* Responsive: Using `marquee` from right to left to the top banner content on tablet and mobile.
* Image background is inside the container (12 columns).

<CodeView codeText={`<TopBanner className="u-backgroundPrimaryLight u-textPrimary" bgImage="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gotitinc/aha-assets/master/gotit/topBanner/bg-1.png" dismissible>
  <div className="u-flex u-alignItemsCenter u-justifyContentCenter">
    Connect anytime to free, instant by installing the Chrome extension
    <div className="u-roundedMedium u-backgroundPrimary u-textWhite u-flexInline u-paddingVerticalTiny u-paddingHorizontalExtraSmall u-textUppercase u-marginLeftMedium">
      <img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gotitinc/aha-assets/master/gotit/topBanner/chrome.svg" alt="" className="u-maxWidthFull u-marginRightExtraSmall" />
      <span>Add to Chome</span>
    </div>
  </div>
</TopBanner>`}

# Top Menu

Source: https://github.com/tutoruniverse/ahaui/blob/main/apps/docs/src/pages/components/top-menu.mdx

title: Top Menu

import ComponentApi from 'src/components/ComponentApi';

import defaultTopMenu from 'src/examples/TopMenu/default';

# Top Menu

## Introduction

Top menu is the main navigation of the site, which is usually accompanied by the logo. Top menu is used to navigate between pages.

<img
  src={require('src/assets/structure/stb_top-menu-structure.jpg')}
  srcSet={`${require('src/assets/structure/stb_top-menu-structure@2x.jpg')} 2x`}
  className="u-maxWidthFull"
  alt="Top Menu"
<ol className="u-textGray u-marginTopTiny">
  <li>
      Label
    <i className="u-text200"> - Concise explanations of the content within.</i>
  </li>
  <li>
      Indicator
    <i className="u-text200"> - A 2px primary color bar that indicates current/active page.</i>
  </li>
  <li>
      Toggle icon
    <i className="u-text200"> - A right-aligned arrow icon used to visualize the sub-menu and provide clickable action to open and close the sub-menu.</i>
  </li>
  <li>
      Badge
    <i className="u-text200"> - An optional right-alined badge contains a status or a numeric value, which indicates a running tally or quantity-based summary.</i>
  </li>
  <li>
      Spacing
    <i className="u-text200"> - The space between nav-items should be 24px at minimum.</i>
  </li>
</ol>

## Examples

### States

#### Normal

The default state of an enable nav-item.

#### Active

The state of the current active nav-item.

#### Disabled

The state indicates that the nav-item cannot be interacted with.

<CodeView codeText={defaultTopMenu} />

## Design Reference

N/A

## API

<ComponentApi metadata={props.data.TopMenu} />
<ComponentApi metadata={props.data.TopMenuItem} exportedBy={props.data.TopMenu} />
<ComponentApi metadata={props.data.TopMenuSubMenu} exportedBy={props.data.TopMenu} />

export const query = graphql`
  query TopMenuQuery {
    TopMenu: componentMetadata(displayName: { eq: "TopMenu" }) {
      ...ComponentApi_metadata
    TopMenuItem: componentMetadata(displayName: { eq: "TopMenuItem" }) {
      ...ComponentApi_metadata
    TopMenuSubMenu: componentMetadata(displayName: { eq: "TopMenuSubMenu" }) {
      ...ComponentApi_metadata
