# Animation

## Introduction

One object should be applied to only one transform. Try to use nested objects for multiple transforms.

## ClassName

<table className="Table Table--layoutFixed u-backgroundWhite u-textDark u-border u-borderTopNone">
    <thead>
        <tr>
            <th>CSS Class</th>
            <th width="140">Preview</th>
            <th>Description</th>
        </tr>
    </thead>
    <tbody>
        {classExtractAnimation.map((item) =>
            item.copy ? (
                <tr key={item.index}>
                    <td
                        colSpan="3"
                        className="u-fontMedium u-backgroundLightest"
                    >
                        {item.copy}
                        <br />
                        <small className="u-fontRegular">
                            {item.description}
                        </small>
                    </td>
                </tr>
            ) : (
                <tr key={item.index}>
                    <td className="u-textNoWrap">
                        <code>{item.className && `.${item.className}`}</code>
                    </td>
                    <td className="u-positionRelative">
                        {item.preview !== false && (
                            <Icon
                                name={item.iconName || "arrowRoundUp"}
                                className={classNames(
                                    item.className && item.className,
                                    item.addClassName && item.addClassName
                                )}
                                size="medium"
                        )}
                    </td>
                    <td className="u-textGray u-text200">{item.description}</td>
                </tr>
            )
        )}
    </tbody>
</table>

<div class="u-text200 u-marginBottomMedium u-marginTopSmall">
    <span class="u-textNegative">*</span>&nbsp;
    <span class="u-fontMedium">Notes:</span>&nbsp;
    <i>
        It's possible to add delays directly on the element's class attribute.
    </i>
</div>

    { className: "u-roundedLeftLarge" },
    { className: "u-roundedRightLarge" },
    { className: "u-roundedExtraLarge" },
    { className: "u-roundedTopExtraLarge" },
    { className: "u-roundedBottomExtraLarge" },
    { className: "u-roundedLeftExtraLarge" },
    { className: "u-roundedRightExtraLarge" },
    { className: "u-roundedCircle" },
];

# Borders

## Introduction

Use border CSS-Utilities to add or remove an element’s borders. Choose from all borders or one at a time.

## ClassName

<table className="Table Table--layoutFixed u-backgroundWhite u-textDark u-border u-borderTopNone">
    <thead>
        <tr>
            <th>CSS Class</th>
            <th width="240">Preview</th>
        </tr>
    </thead>
    <tbody>
        {classExtractBorders.map((item) =>
            item.copy ? (
                <tr key={item.index}>
                    <td
                        colSpan="2"
                        className="u-fontMedium u-backgroundLightest"
                    >
                        {item.copy}
                    </td>
                </tr>
            ) : (
                <tr key={item.index}>
                    <td className="u-textNoWrap">
                        <code>
                            {item.className
                                ? `.${item.className}`
                                : ".u-border"}
                        </code>
                    </td>
                    <td className="u-positionRelative">
                        <div
                            className={classNames(
                                "u-marginExtraSmall u-positionAbsolute u-positionFull u-backgroundOpaline",
                                !item.noDefault && "u-border ",
                                item.className && item.className
                            )}
                            style={{
                                width:
                                    item.className === "u-roundedCircle"
                                        ? 32
                                        : undefined,
                                height:
                                    item.className === "u-roundedCircle"
                                        ? 32
                                        : undefined,
                            }}
                        ></div>
                    </td>
                </tr>
            )
        )}
    </tbody>
</table>

## Hover

Convey meaning through color with a handful of color utility classes. Includes support for styling links with hover states, too.

<p>
    Example: &nbsp;
    <code class="u-borderBottom hover:u-borderPrimary">
        .hover:u-borderPrimary
    </code>
</p>

## Responsive classes

The border color and border side includes six tiers of predefined classes for building complex responsive colors and sides. Customize the color or sides of your component on extra small, small, medium, large, or extra large devices however you see fit.

-   `sm:u-borderX` - To use at the smallest Media Query breakpoint.
-   `md:u-borderX` - To use at the medium Media Query breakpoint.
-   `lg:u-borderX` - To use at the large Media Query breakpoint.
-   `xl:u-borderX` - To use at the extra large or desktop Media Query breakpoint.
-   `xxl:u-borderX` - To use at the monitor Media Query breakpoint.

---

# Box Shadow

Source: https://github.com/tutoruniverse/ahaui/blob/main/apps/docs/src/pages/css-utilities/box-shadow.mdx

title: Box Shadow
import classNames from 'classnames';

export const classExtractBoxShadow = [
  { className: 'u-shadowSmall' },
  { className: 'u-shadowMedium' },
  { className: 'u-shadowLarge' },
  { className: 'u-shadowExtraLarge' },
  { className: 'u-shadowNone' },
  { className: 'focus:u-shadowOutline', clickAble: true },
];

# Box Shadow

## Introduction

Add or remove shadows to elements with box-shadow CSS-Utilities.

## ClassName
<table className="Table Table--layoutFixed u-backgroundWhite u-textDark u-border u-borderTopNone">
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th>CSS Class</th>
      <th width="240">Preview</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    {classExtractBoxShadow.map((item) => {
      const Component = item.clickAble ? 'button' : 'div';
      return (
        <tr key={item.index}>
          <td className="u-textNoWrap">
            <code>.{item.className}</code>
          </td>
          <td className="u-positionRelative u-paddingExtraSmall u-flex">
            <Component
              className={classNames(
                'u-marginExtraSmall u-paddingVerticalSmall u-backgroundOpaline u-sizeFill',
                item.clickAble && 'u-border',
                item.className && item.className
              )}
          </td>
        </tr>
      );
    })}
  </tbody>
</table>

## Hover

Convey meaning through opacity with a handful of shadow utility classes. Includes support for styling links with hover states, too.

Example: &nbsp;<code className="hover:u-shadowLarge">.hover:u-shadowLarge</code>

# Colors

## Introduction

Contextual text classes also work well on anchors with the provided hover and focus states.

## ClassName

<table className="Table Table--layoutFixed u-backgroundWhite u-textDark u-border u-borderTopNone">
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th width="300">CSS Class</th>
      <th>Preview</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    {classExtractColors.map(item => (
      item.copy ? (
        <tr key={item.index}>
          <td colSpan="2" className="u-fontMedium u-backgroundLightest">
            {item.copy}
          </td>
        </tr>
      ):(
        <tr key={item.index}>
          <td className="u-textNoWrap">
            <code>.{item.classText || item.classBackground }</code>
          </td>
          <td className="u-positionRelative">
            <div
              className={classNames(
                'u-marginExtraSmall',
                item.classBackground && item.classBackground,
                item.classText && item.classText,
                !item.classText && 'u-positionAbsolute u-positionFull'
              )}
            >
              {item.classText && 'The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog'}
            </div>
          </td>
        </tr>
      )
    ))}
  </tbody>
</table>

## Hover
Convey meaning through color with a handful of color utility classes. Includes support for styling links with hover states, too.

Both of text and background have the default and `:hover`  states ( except *Color palette background
*).

Replace .u-text** to u-background** when use *Color palette background* as text color.

<p>Example: &nbsp;<code class="hover:u-textDark">.hover:u-textDark</code>&nbsp;<code class="hover:u-backgroundPrimary">.hover:u-backgroundPrimary</code></p>

# Cursors

Source: https://github.com/tutoruniverse/ahaui/blob/main/apps/docs/src/pages/css-utilities/cursors.mdx

title: Cursors
import classNames from 'classnames';

export const classExtractCursors = [
  { className: 'u-cursorDefault', description: 'The default cursor' },
  { className: 'u-cursorPointer', description: 'The cursor is a pointer and indicates a link' },
  { className: 'u-cursorMove', description: 'The cursor indicates something is to be moved' },
  { className: 'u-cursorNotAllow', description: 'The cursor indicates that the requested action will not be executed' },
  { className: 'u-cursorHelp', description: 'The cursor indicates that help is available' },
  { className: 'u-cursorProgress', description: 'The cursor indicates that the program is busy (in progress)' },
  { className: 'u-cursorGrab', description: 'The cursor indicates that something can be grabbed' },
  { className: 'u-cursorGrabbing', description: 'The cursor indicates that something can be grabbed' },
  { className: 'u-cursorZoomIn', description: 'The cursor indicates that something can be zoomed in' },
  { className: 'u-cursorZoomOut', description: 'The cursor indicates that something can be zoomed out' },
  { className: 'u-cursorColResize', description: 'The cursor indicates that the column can be resized horizontally' },
  { className: 'u-cursorRowResize', description: 'The cursor indicates that the row can be resized vertically' },
  { className: 'u-cursorEwResize', description: 'Indicates a bidirectional resize cursor' },
  { className: 'u-cursorNsResize', description: 'Indicates a bidirectional resize cursor' },
];

# Cursors

## Introduction

Use the CSS-Utility cursor to control the cursor style when hovering over an element.

## ClassName

<table className="Table Table--layoutFixed u-backgroundWhite u-textDark u-border u-borderTopNone">
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th width="200">CSS Class</th>
      <th width="140">Preview</th>
      <th>Description</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    {classExtractCursors.map(item => (
      <tr key={item.index}>
        <td className="u-textNoWrap">
          <code>.{item.className}</code>
        </td>
        <td className="u-positionRelative">
          <div
            className={classNames(
              'u-marginExtraSmall u-positionAbsolute u-positionFull u-backgroundOpaline u-flex u-alignItemsCenter u-justifyContentCenter u-border',
              item.className && item.className
            )}
          >
            Hover me !
          </div>
        </td>
        <td className="u-textGray">
          {item.description}
        </td>
      </tr>
    ))}
  </tbody>
</table>

# Display

Source: https://github.com/tutoruniverse/ahaui/blob/main/apps/docs/src/pages/css-utilities/display.mdx

title: Display

import inline from 'src/examples/CSS/Display/inline';
import inlineBlock from 'src/examples/CSS/Display/inlineBlock';
import block from 'src/examples/CSS/Display/block';
import flex from 'src/examples/CSS/Display/flex';
import flexInline from 'src/examples/CSS/Display/flexInline';
import hidden from 'src/examples/CSS/Display/hidden';
import table from 'src/examples/CSS/Display/table';
import responsive from 'src/examples/CSS/Display/responsive';

# Display

## Introduction

The default display value for most elements is block or inline.

A block-level element always starts on a new line and takes up the full width available. An inline element does not start on a new line and only takes up as much width as necessary.

## Examples

### Inline

Class: `.u-inline`

<CodeView codeText={inline} />

### Inline block

Class: `.u-inlineBlock`

<CodeView codeText={inlineBlock} />

### Block

Class: `.u-block`

<CodeView codeText={block} />

### Flex

Class: `.u-flex`. See more about Flexbox.

<CodeView codeText={flex} />

### Inline flex

Class: `.u-flexInline`

<CodeView codeText={flexInline} />

### Hidden

Class: `.u-hidden`. Use to hide elements without deleting and recreating them. In this example, the item "Two" is hidden.

<CodeView codeText={hidden} />

### Table

Classes: `.u-table`, `.u-tableRow`, `.u-tableCell`. Use some "div" tags to make a table.

<CodeView codeText={table} />

## Responsive display

<table className="Table u-backgroundWhite u-borderLeft  u-borderRight  u-borderBottom">
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th width="200">Screen Size</th>
      <th>Class</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr>
      <td colSpan="2" className="u-backgroundLightest">
        <strong>Hidden:</strong>
      </td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Hidden on all</td>
      <td><code>.u-hidden</code></td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Hidden only on sm</td>
      <td><code>.sm:u-hidden .md:u-block</code></td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Hidden only on md</td>
      <td><code>.md:u-hidden .lg:u-block</code></td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Hidden only on lg</td>
      <td><code>.lg:u-hidden .xl:u-block</code></td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Hidden only on xl</td>
      <td><code>.xl:u-hidden</code></td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td colSpan="2" className="u-backgroundLightest">
        <strong>Visible:</strong>
      </td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Visible on all</td>
      <td><code>.u-block</code></td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Visible only on sm</td>
      <td><code>.u-hidden .sm:u-block .md:u-hidden</code></td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Visible only on md</td>
      <td><code>.u-hidden .md:u-block .lg:u-hidden</code></td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Visible only on lg</td>
      <td><code>.u-hidden .lg:u-block .xl:u-hidden</code></td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Visible only on xl</td>
      <td><code>.u-hidden .xl:u-block</code></td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
Resize the browser to see the change:

<CodeView codeText={responsive} />

# Filter and Backdrop Filter

Source: https://github.com/tutoruniverse/ahaui/blob/main/apps/docs/src/pages/css-utilities/filters.mdx

title: Filters
import classNames from 'classnames';

export const classFilterGrayscale = [
  { className: 'u-grayscale', description: 'Change all images to black and white (100% gray)' },
  { className: 'u-grayscaleNone', description: 'Reset to the original image' },
  { className: 'hover:u-grayscale', description: 'Mouse hover: Change all images to black and white' },
  { className: 'u-grayscale hover:u-grayscaleNone', description: 'Mouse hover: Reset to the original image' },
];

export const classBackdropFilterBlur = [
  { className: 'u-backdropBlurSmall', description: '' },
  { className: 'u-backdropBlurMedium', description: '' },
  { className: 'u-backdropBlurLarge', description: '' },
  { className: 'u-backdropBlurNone', description: '' },
];

export const classBackdropFilterGrayscale = [
  { className: 'u-backdropGrayscale', description: '' },
  { className: 'u-backdropGrayscaleNone', description: '' },
];

# Filter and Backdrop Filter

## Filter

The `filter` property is the CSS way of applying filter effects to elements on a web page (mostly images).

### Grayscale

<div class="u-border u-paddingMedium u-marginBottomLarge">
  <div className="Grid">
    {classFilterGrayscale.map(item => (
      <div key={item.index} className="u-sizeFull md:u-size1of4 u-marginBottomMedium">
        <img src={require("src/assets/demo/flower.jpg")}
          className={classNames('u-block u-widthFull u-transitionAll u-duration100 u-easeInOut', item.className && item.className)}
          title="" />
        <div className="u-marginVerticalExtraSmall"><code>.{item.className}</code></div>
        <div className="u-textGray">{item.description}</div>
      </div>
    ))}
  </div>
</div>

## Backdrop Filter

The `backdrop-filter` CSS property lets you apply graphical effects such as blurring or color shifting to the area behind an element. Because it applies to everything behind the element, to see the effect you must make the element or its background at least partially transparent.

### Grayscale

<div
  class="u-border u-paddingExtraLarge u-backgroundCover u-backgroundFixed u-textCenter u-marginBottomLarge"
  style={{ backgroundImage: `url(${require("src/assets/demo/flower.jpg")})` }}
>
  <div className="Grid">
    {classBackdropFilterGrayscale.map(item => (
      <div key={item.index} className="u-sizeFull md:u-size1of2 u-marginVerticalLarge">
        <div className={classNames(
          'u-border u-paddingVerticalExtraLarge',
          item.className && item.className
          )}
        >
          <div class="u-inlineBlock u-paddingTiny u-backgroundWhite">
            <code>.{item.className}</code>
          </div>
          {/* <div>{item.description}</div> */}
        </div>
      </div>
    ))}
  </div>
</div>

### Blur

<div
  class="u-border u-paddingExtraLarge u-backgroundCover u-backgroundFixed u-textCenter u-marginBottomLarge"
  style={{ backgroundImage: `url(${require("src/assets/demo/flower.jpg")})` }}
>
  <div className="Grid">
    {classBackdropFilterBlur.map(item => (
      <div key={item.index} className="u-sizeFull md:u-size1of2 u-marginVerticalLarge">
        <div className={classNames(
          'u-border u-paddingVerticalExtraLarge',
          item.className && item.className
          )}
        >
          <div class="u-inlineBlock u-paddingTiny u-backgroundWhite">
            <code>.{item.className}</code>
          </div>
          {/* <div>{item.description}</div> */}
        </div>
      </div>
    ))}
  </div>
</div>

# Object Fit

Source: https://github.com/tutoruniverse/ahaui/blob/main/apps/docs/src/pages/css-utilities/object-fit.mdx

title: Object Fit
import classNames from 'classnames';

export const classExtractCursors = [
  { className: 'u-objectContain', description: 'The replaced content is scaled to maintain its aspect ratio while fitting within the element’s content box. The entire object is made to fill the box, while preserving its aspect ratio, so the object will be "letterboxed" if its aspect ratio does not match the aspect ratio of the box.' },
  { className: 'u-objectCover', description: 'The replaced content is sized to maintain its aspect ratio while filling the element’s entire content box. If the object\'s aspect ratio does not match the aspect ratio of its box, then the object will be clipped to fit.' },
  { className: 'u-objectFill', description: 'The replaced content is sized to fill the element’s content box. The entire object will completely fill the box. If the object\'s aspect ratio does not match the aspect ratio of its box, then the object will be stretched to fit.' },
  { className: 'u-objectScaleDown', description: 'The content is sized as if none or contain were specified, whichever would result in a smaller concrete object size.' },
  { className: 'u-objectNone', description: 'The replaced content is not resized.' },
];

# Object Fit

## Introduction

The object-fit CSS property sets how the content of a replaced element, such as an `<img>` or `<video>`, should be resized to fit its container.

## ClassName

<table className="Table Table--layoutFixed u-backgroundWhite u-textDark u-border u-borderTopNone">
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th width="200">CSS Class</th>
      <th>Preview</th>
      <th width="320">Description</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    {classExtractCursors.map(item => (
      <tr key={item.index}>
        <td className="u-textNoWrap">
          <code>.{item.className}</code>
        </td>
        <td className="u-positionRelative">
          <div
            className={classNames(
              'u-backgroundLighter u-border borderGray'
            )}
          >
            <img
              src={require('src/assets/demo/cat.jpg')}
              className={classNames(
                'u-block u-widthFull u-heightHuge',
                item.className && item.className
              )}
              style={{ }}
              alt="Spot illustrations"
          </div>
        </td>
        <td className="u-textGray">
          {item.description}
        </td>
      </tr>
    ))}
  </tbody>
</table>

# Opacity

Source: https://github.com/tutoruniverse/ahaui/blob/main/apps/docs/src/pages/css-utilities/opacities.mdx

title: Opacities
import classNames from 'classnames';

export const classExtractOpacity = [
  { className: 'u-opacityNone' },
  { className: 'u-opacityQuarter' },
  { className: 'u-opacityHalf' },
  { className: 'u-opacityThreeQuarter' },
  { className: 'u-opacityReset' },
];

# Opacity

## Introduction

Use the CSS-Utility opacity to control the opacity of an element.

## ClassName

<table className="Table Table--layoutFixed u-backgroundWhite u-textDark u-border u-borderTopNone">
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th>CSS Class</th>
      <th width="240">Preview</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    {classExtractOpacity.map(item => (
      <tr key={item.index}>
        <td className="u-textNoWrap">
          <code>.{item.className ? item.className : 'u-border'}</code>
        </td>
        <td className="u-positionRelative">
          <div
            className={classNames(
              'u-marginExtraSmall u-positionAbsolute u-positionFull u-backgroundGray',
              !item.noDefault && 'u-border ',
              item.className && item.className
            )}
        </td>
      </tr>
    ))}
  </tbody>
</table>

## Hover

Convey meaning through opacity with a handful of opacity utility classes. Includes support for styling links with hover states, too.

Example: &nbsp;<code className="hover:u-opacityThreeQuarter">.hover:u-opacityThreeQuarter</code>

# Position

Source: https://github.com/tutoruniverse/ahaui/blob/main/apps/docs/src/pages/css-utilities/position.mdx

title: Position

import absoluteSingle from 'src/examples/CSS/Position/absoluteSingle';
import absoluteTop from 'src/examples/CSS/Position/absoluteTop';
import absoluteRight from 'src/examples/CSS/Position/absoluteRight';
import absoluteBottom from 'src/examples/CSS/Position/absoluteBottom';
import absoluteLeft from 'src/examples/CSS/Position/absoluteLeft';
import absoluteCenter from 'src/examples/CSS/Position/absoluteCenter';
import absoluteMixed from 'src/examples/CSS/Position/absoluteMixed';
//import sticky from 'src/examples/CSS/Position/sticky';
import fixed from 'src/examples/CSS/Position/fixed';

# Position

## Examples

### Relative and Absolute

Absolute (`.u-positionAbsolute`) elements should be in side a relative (`.u-positionRelative`) element.

### Corners
* Top-Left: `.u-positionAbsolute .u-positionTop .u-positionLeft`
* Top-Right: `.u-positionAbsolute .u-positionTop .u-positionRight`
* Bottom-Left: `.u-positionAbsolute .u-positionBottom .u-positionLeft`
* Bottom-Right: `.u-positionAbsolute .u-positionBottom .u-positionRight`
* Center: `.u-positionAbsolute .u-positionCenter`
* Horizontal Center: `.u-positionAbsolute .u-positionHorizontalCenter`
* Vertical Center: `.u-positionAbsolute .u-positionVerticalCenter`
* Full: `.u-positionAbsolute .u-positionFull`

<CodeView codeText={absoluteSingle} />

### Directions

#### Top

<CodeView codeText={absoluteTop} />

#### Bottom

<CodeView codeText={absoluteBottom} />

#### Left

<CodeView codeText={absoluteLeft} />

#### Right

<CodeView codeText={absoluteRight} />

#### Center

<CodeView codeText={absoluteCenter} />

### Sides

* Top: `.u-positionAbsolute .u-positionTop .u-positionLeft .u-positionRight`
* Right: `.u-positionAbsolute .u-positionRight .u-positionTop .u-positionBottom`
* Bottom: `.u-positionAbsolute .u-positionBottom .u-positionLeft .u-positionRight`
* Left: `.u-positionAbsolute .u-positionLeft .u-positionTop .u-positionBottom`

<CodeView codeText={absoluteMixed} />

### Fixed

See the blue bar at the bottom

<CodeView codeText={fixed} />

# Spacing

## CSS Box Model

The CSS box model is essentially a box that wraps around every HTML element. It consists of: margins, borders, padding, and the actual content.

<div className="u-marginBottomMedium u-backgroundWarningLight u-border u-borderDashed u-borderGray u-paddingVerticalTiny u-paddingHorizontalSmall u-textCenter">
  margin
  <div className="u-backgroundBlack u-paddingVerticalTiny u-paddingHorizontalSmall">
    <span className="u-textWhite">border</span>
    <div className="u-backgroundPositiveLight u-paddingVerticalTiny u-paddingHorizontalSmall">
      padding
      <div className="u-backgroundWhite u-paddingSmall">
        Content
      </div>
        &nbsp;
    </div>
      &nbsp;
  </div>
    &nbsp;
</div>

## Padding and Margin

Assign responsive-friendly `margin` or `padding` values to an element or a subset of its sides with shorthand classes. Includes support for individual properties, all properties, and vertical and horizontal properties. Classes are built from a default Sass map ranging from `4px` to `96px`.

The classes are named using the format `.u-{property}{sides}{size}`  for `xs` and  `.{breakpoint}:u-{property}{sides}{size}`  for `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xl`, and `xxl`.

### Sides

<table className="Table Table--layoutFixed u-backgroundWhite u-textDark u-border u-borderTopNone">
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th>CSS Class</th>
      <th width="240">Preview</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    {classExtractSides.map(item => (
      item.copy ? (
        <tr key={item.index}>
          <td colSpan="2" className="u-fontMedium u-backgroundLightest">
            {item.copy}
          </td>
        </tr>
      ) : (
        <tr key={item.index}>
          <td className="u-textNoWrap">
            <code>
              {item.className && `.${item.className}`}
            </code>
          </td>
          <td className="u-positionRelative u-marginExtraSmall">
            <div className={classNames(
                'u-border u-inlineBlock u-lineHeightNone',
                item.margin ? 'u-backgroundWarningLighter': 'u-backgroundPositiveLight'
              )}>
              <div
                className={classNames(
                  'u-inlineBlock',
                  item.className && item.className
                )}
                >
                <div className="u-backgroundOpaline" style={{
                  width: 32 ,
                  height: 24,
                }}/>
              </div>
            </div>
          </td>
        </tr>
      )
    ))}
  </tbody>
</table>

### Available classes

<table className="Table Table--layoutFixed u-backgroundWhite u-textDark u-border u-borderTopNone">
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th>CSS Class</th>
      <th>Description</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    {classExtractSpaceAllSides.map(item => (
      item.copy ? (
        <tr key={item.index}>
          <td colSpan="2" className="u-fontMedium u-backgroundLightest">
            {item.copy}
          </td>
        </tr>
      ) : (
        <tr key={item.index}>
          <td className="u-textNoWrap">
            <code>
              {item.className && `.${item.className}`}
            </code>
          </td>
          <td className="u-textGray u-text200">
            {item.description}
          </td>
        </tr>
      )
    ))}
  </tbody>
</table>

### Responsive classes
The padding and margin includes six tiers of predefined classes for building complex responsive spacing. Customize the space of your component on extra small, small, medium, large, or extra large devices however you see fit.

* `sm:u-margin/paddingX`  - To use at the smallest Media Query breakpoint.
* `md:u-margin/paddingX`  - To use at the medium Media Query breakpoint.
* `lg:u-margin/paddingX`  - To use at the large Media Query breakpoint.
* `xl:u-margin/paddingX`  - To use at the extra large or desktop Media Query breakpoint.
* `xxl:u-margin/paddingX`  - To use at the monitor Media Query breakpoint.

# SVG

Source: https://github.com/tutoruniverse/ahaui/blob/main/apps/docs/src/pages/css-utilities/svg.mdx

title: SVG
import classNames from 'classnames';
import { Icon } from '@ahaui/react';

# SVG

CSS Utilities for SVG

## Fill

Use the <code>.u-fillCurrent</code> class to set the fill color of an SVG to the current text color, or use the <code>.u-fillNone</code> class to set its fill color to transparent.

<div className="u-positionRelative u-border u-borderUltraLight u-paddingMedium u-marginBottomLarge">
  <div class="u-marginBottomMedium">
    <Icon size="extraLarge" name="thumbsUp" className="u-textPositive u-fillCurrent" />
    <div><code>.u-textPositive .u-fillCurrent</code></div>
  </div>
  <div class="u-marginBottomMedium">
    <Icon size="extraLarge" name="thumbsUp" className="u-textPrimary u-fillCurrent" />
    <div><code>.u-textPrimary .u-fillCurrent</code></div>
  </div>
  <div class="u-marginBottomMedium">
    <span class="u-inlineBlock u-border u-borderDashed">
      <Icon size="extraLarge" name="thumbsUp" className="u-fillNone" />
    </span>
    <div><code>.u-fillNone</code></div>
  </div>
</div>

## Stroke

Use the <code>.u-strokeCurrent</code> class to set the stroke color of an SVG to the current text color. Also add the <code>.u-fillNone</code> to remove the fill color.

<div className="u-positionRelative u-border u-borderUltraLight u-paddingMedium u-marginBottomLarge">
  <div class="u-marginBottomMedium">
    <Icon size="extraLarge" name="thumbsUp" className="u-textPrimary u-strokeCurrent u-fillNone" />
    <div><code>.u-textPrimary .u-fillNone .u-strokeCurrent</code></div>
  </div>
  <div class="u-marginBottomMedium">
    <Icon size="extraLarge" name="thumbsUp" className="u-textPrimary u-strokeCurrent u-stroke-2 u-fillNone" />
    <div><code>.u-textPrimary .u-fillNone .u-strokeCurrent .u-stroke-2</code></div>
  </div>
</div>

# Text

Text is the main object in chat application as our products. We defined a collection of typography which is optimized to be highly legible, performs well in our products.

## Font family

We use sans serif font and [Roboto][1] font is chosen for our type. Beside that, we also use Courier font for visualize code.

## Link

Use when you are linking just a few words of text, or when a link is standalone. Do not use for actions, instead use a button. Links use `B300` color and are not underlined except on hover.

<CodeView codeText={`<>
  <p>Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet <a href="#" title="Hyperlink">hyperlink</a> sed do eiusmod tempor incididunt</p>
  <p><a href="#" title="Home">Home</a></p>
  <p><a href="#" title="About">Go Back</a></p>
</>`}/>

## Paragraph

<CodeView codeText={`<>
  <p>Lorem ipsum is placeholder text commonly used in the graphic, print, and publishing industries for previewing layouts and visual mockups.</p>
  <p>Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit, sed do eiusmod tempor incididunt ut labore et dolore magna aliqua. Ut enim ad minim veniam, quis nostrud exercitation ullamco laboris nisi ut aliquip ex ea commodo consequat. Duis aute irure dolor in reprehenderit in voluptate velit esse cillum dolore eu fugiat nulla pariatur. Excepteur sint occaecat cupidatat non proident, sunt in culpa qui officia deserunt mollit anim id est laborum.</p>
</>`}/>

## More Examples

<table className="Table Table--layoutFixed u-backgroundWhite u-textDark u-border u-borderTopNone">
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th scope="col">CSS className</th>
      <th scope="col">Properties</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  {textOthers.map(item => (
    <tbody>
      {item.className ? (
        !item.deprecated && (
        <tr key={item.index}>
          <td className="u-textNoWrap">
            <code>
              .
              {item.className}
            </code>
            {/* {item.deprecated === true ? <div><Badge variant="negative_subtle">deprecated</Badge></div> : '' } */}
            {item.tag ? (
              <div>
                <small>Tag:</small>
                {' '}
                <code>{item.tag}</code>
              </div>
            ) : ''}
          </td>
          <td>
            <div className={item.className}>
              {item.copy}
            </div>
          </td>
          <td className="u-textGray u-text200">
            {item.description}
          </td>
        </tr>
        )
      ) : (
        <tr key={item.index}>
          <td colSpan="3" className="u-fontMedium u-backgroundLightest">
            {item.copy}
          </td>
        </tr>
      )}
    </tbody>
  ))}
</table>

[1]: https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Roboto?selection.family=Roboto:wght@400;500;700&query=roboto&sidebar.open

# User Select

Source: https://github.com/tutoruniverse/ahaui/blob/main/apps/docs/src/pages/css-utilities/user-select.mdx

title: User Select
import classNames from 'classnames';

export const classExtractCursors = [
  { className: 'u-userSelectAuto', description: 'Default. Text can be selected if the browser allows it' },
  { className: 'u-userSelectNone', description: 'Prevent text selection	' },
  { className: 'u-userSelectText', description: 'The text can be selected by the user' },
  { className: 'u-userSelectAll', description: 'Text selection is made with one click instead of a double-click' },
];

# User Select

## Introduction

Use the CSS-Utility user-select to control the text of an element can be selected.

## ClassName

<table className="Table Table--layoutFixed u-backgroundWhite u-textDark u-border u-borderTopNone">
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th width="200">CSS Class</th>
      <th width="140">Preview</th>
      <th>Description</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    {classExtractCursors.map(item => (
      <tr key={item.index}>
        <td className="u-textNoWrap">
          <code>.{item.className}</code>
        </td>
        <td className="u-positionRelative">
          <div
            className={classNames(
              'u-marginExtraSmall u-positionAbsolute u-positionFull u-flex u-alignItemsCenter u-justifyContentCenter u-paddingHorizontalSmall u-textNoWrap',
              item.className && item.className
            )}
          >
            Double-click me!
          </div>
        </td>
        <td className="u-textGray">
          {item.description}
        </td>
      </tr>
    ))}
  </tbody>
</table>

# Colors

Color palette listings and general guide to use colors in product design.

## Guideline

### Primary colors

<div className="Grid Grid--smallGutter u-marginBottomExtraSmall">
  {blockColor.primary.map(item => (
    <div key={item.title} className="u-sizeFull md:u-size1of2 xl:u-size2of8 u-marginBottomMedium">
      {renderBlockColor(item, 'u-paddingHorizontalExtraSmall u-paddingBottomTiny u-paddingTopMedium')}
    </div>
  ))}
</div>

Our primary palette is comprised of blue, dark neutral, white, and orange. These colors are present across most touch points from marketing to product.

* Blue Blue300 -  `#375DE7` is used for primary actions and buttons, links, for indicating progress, and representing authentication.
* Dark neutral Neutral800 -  `#172B4D`  is used primarily for body text and headings.
* White White -  `#FFFFFF`  is used for page backgrounds and anything that is white.
* Orange Orange300 -  `#ED6200`  is used like accent color for ask flow and payment flow.

### Secondary colors

<div className="Grid Grid--smallGutter u-marginBottomExtraSmall">
  {blockColor.secondary.map(item => (
    <div key={item.title} className="u-sizeFull md:u-size1of2 xl:u-size2of8 u-marginBottomMedium">
      {renderBlockColor(item, 'u-paddingHorizontalExtraSmall u-paddingBottomTiny u-paddingTopSmall')}
    </div>
  ))}
</div>

### Neutrals

There are various shades of neutral colors. They are used for text and subtle backgrounds when we don't want to make too much attention to less important information or convey information such as `disabled`.

* Red Red300 -  `#D0021B`  is used for negative alerts and messages.
* Yellow Yellow300 -  `#FFAB00` is used for warning alerts and messages.
* Green Green300 -  `#E3B000`  is used for positive notications and messages.

<div className="Grid Grid--smallGutter u-marginBottomExtraSmall">
  {blockColor.neutrals.map(item => (
    <div key={item.key} className="u-sizeFull md:u-size1of2 xl:u-size4of12 xxl:u-size2of8 u-marginBottomMedium">
      <h6 className="u-marginBottomExtraSmall">{item.title}</h6>
      {item.list.map(color => (
        <React.Fragment key={color.title}>
          {renderBlockColor(color, 'u-paddingHorizontalExtraSmall u-paddingVerticalTiny u-marginBottomTiny')}
        </React.Fragment>
      ))}
    </div>
  ))}
</div>

### Extended palette

Extended palette is all the useable tints and shades of each color in the palette. It can be used for background, illustrations and components in product.

<div className="Grid Grid--smallGutter u-marginBottomExtraSmall">
  {blockColor.extended.map(item => (
    <div key={item.key} className="u-sizeFull md:u-size1of2 xl:u-size4of12 xxl:u-size2of8 u-marginBottomMedium">
      <h6 className="u-marginBottomExtraSmall">{item.title}</h6>
      {item.list.map(color => (
        <React.Fragment key={color.title}>
          {renderBlockColor(color, 'u-paddingHorizontalExtraSmall u-paddingVerticalTiny u-marginBottomTiny')}
        </React.Fragment>
      ))}
    </div>
  ))}
</div>

# Illustration Style Guidelines

Source: https://github.com/tutoruniverse/ahaui/blob/main/apps/docs/src/pages/foundations/illustration.mdx

title: Illustration

# Illustration Style Guidelines

## Introduction

<p className="u-textCenter">
  <img
    src={require('src/assets/structure/stb_illustration_introduction.png')}
    className="u-maxWidthFull"
    style={{ height: 260 }}
    alt="Introduction"
</p>

Create a visually appealing style that works across character, scene and spot illustrations. Illustrations should make users feel more clear in their tasks and confident to active. The illustrations should be consistent as they came from the same source— the same brand, the same voice, the same person (metaphorically, and literally look like they were illustrated by one person)—while still smoothly changing tone, depending on the audience, their task, and emotional state.

### Visual Principles

* Clarity, Efficiency, Consistency, Professional
* No gaudy or flashy, non-showbiz

### Storytelling guidelines

**Overall**

* Flat design - save time for designers, easy for animated, support SVG
* Focus on using original shapes, and light colors
* Keep it simple. Symbolism

## Sizes

### Spot illustrations

<p className="u-textCenter">
  <img
    src={require('src/assets/structure/stb_illustration_spot.png')}
    className="u-maxWidthFull"
    style={{ height: 120 }}
    alt="Spot illustrations"
</p>

Spot illustrations are the simplest and most literal expression of a concept. A spot illustration is used to help showcase a small feature or explain an experience. They’re lightweight, not too busy but are there to help enhance the flow by bringing the interface to life and delighting the user.

### Spot Hero illustrations

<p className="u-textCenter">
  <img
    src={require('src/assets/structure/stb_illustration_spot-hero.png')}
    className="u-maxWidthFull"
    style={{ height: 340 }}
    alt="Spot Hero illustrations"
</p>

Smaller size than Hero, focus on a single vignette. These assets are perfect when you need to pack a punch with limited space. Often, they are slightly more literal representations of a single concept. Despite simplification, they still contain a small team working on or around a larger-than-life subject.

### Hero illustrations

<p className="u-textCenter">
  <img
    src={require('src/assets/structure/stb_illustration_hero.png')}
    className="u-maxWidthFull"
    style={{ height: 340 }}
    alt="Hero illustrations"
</p>

A hero illustration works on a larger space and allows the user to explain a feature or a scenario with a more detailed driven approach by more complex elements.

## Color palette

The color palette and other details were based on branding to look consistent and work well with product designs.

<p className="u-textCenter">
  <img
    src={require('src/assets/structure/stb_illustration_color.png')}
    className="u-maxWidthFull"
    style={{ height: 120 }}
    alt="Color palette"
</p>

### General Illustrations

To avoid distracting user focus on the product design, illustrations need to keep color balance. We try to lean on our Neutral colors as much as possible, only introducing the rest of the colour palette to give the illustration balance. Neutral 40 is our most frequent colour choice. To highlight, try to use Primary color for the key elements in the illustration.

<table className="Table Table--small Table--bordered u-backgroundWhite u-textDark u-text200">
  <tbody>
    <tr>
      <td>
        Primary color
      </td>
      <td>
        B300 &nbsp;
        <span className="u-textWhite" style={{ backgroundColor: '#375DE7' }}>#375DE7</span>
      </td>
      <td>15%</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>
        Secondary color
      </td>
      <td>
        Lighter blue &nbsp;
        <span className="u-textWhite" style={{ backgroundColor: '#96BAFF' }}>#96BAFF</span>
      </td>
      <td>15%</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>
        Neutral colors
      </td>
      <td>
        White &nbsp;
        <span style={{ color: '#000' }}>#FFFFFF</span>
,
        N40 &nbsp;
        <span style={{ backgroundColor: '#DFE1E6' }}>#DFE1E6</span>
,
N70 &nbsp;
        <span style={{ backgroundColor: '#A5ADBA' }}>#A5ADBA</span>
,
        N900 &nbsp;
        <span className="u-textWhite" style={{ backgroundColor: '#091E42' }}>#091E42</span>
      </td>
      <td>70%</td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

### Message Illustrations

In some cases, there are some message colors are used to add more in the illustrations which helped to make more sense and more attention for the messages.

<table className="Table Table--small Table--bordered u-backgroundWhite u-textDark u-text200">
  <tbody>
    <tr>
      <td>
        Message colors
      </td>
      <td>
        R300 &nbsp;
        <span className="u-textWhite" style={{ backgroundColor: '#D0021B' }}>#D0021B</span>
,
        Y200 &nbsp;
        <span style={{ backgroundColor: '#FFC400' }}>#FFC400</span>
,
        G300 &nbsp;
        <span className="u-textWhite" style={{ backgroundColor: '#22A861' }}>#22A861</span>
      </td>
      <td>30%</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>
        Neutral colors
      </td>
      <td>
        White &nbsp;
        <span style={{ color: '#000' }}>#FFFFFF</span>
,
        N40 &nbsp;
        <span style={{ backgroundColor: '#DFE1E6' }}>#DFE1E6</span>
,
N70 &nbsp;
        <span style={{ backgroundColor: '#A5ADBA' }}>#A5ADBA</span>
,
        N900 &nbsp;
        <span className="u-textWhite" style={{ backgroundColor: '#091E42' }}>#091E42</span>
      </td>
      <td>70%</td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

### Empty State Illustrations

We only use White along with Neutral N40 and N70. We allow for the Solid Stroke option but never use any other colours.

<table className="Table Table--small Table--bordered u-backgroundWhite u-textDark u-text200">
  <tbody>
    <tr>
      <td>
        Neutral colors
      </td>
      <td>
        White &nbsp;
        <span style={{ color: '#000' }}>#FFFFFF</span>
,
        N40 &nbsp;
        <span style={{ backgroundColor: '#DFE1E6' }}>#DFE1E6</span>
      </td>
      <td>70%</td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

<p className="u-textCenter">
  <img
    src={require('src/assets/structure/stb_illustration_color-do-dont.png')}
    className="u-maxWidthFull"
    style={{ height: 240 }}
    alt="illustrations"
</p>

### Shapes

<p className="u-textCenter">
  <img
    src={require('src/assets/structure/stb_illustration_shapes.png')}
    className="u-maxWidthFull"
    style={{ height: 240 }}
    alt="Shapes illustrations"
</p>

* Using organic shapes: circle, square, rectangle, triangle.
* Flexible use of shapes to ensure that the contrast between curves and straight lines.
* Re-used the shape of the product logo for all chat illustrations.
* Shape types:
  * stroke (round) + no fill
  * non-stroke + fill

### Lines

<p className="u-textCenter">
  <img
    src={require('src/assets/structure/stb_illustration_stroke-breakdown.png')}
    className="u-maxWidthFull"
    style={{ height: 240 }}
    alt="Lines illustrations"
</p>

We use a consistent default smooth brush with a 2px stroke. We also allow for 1px stroke if there are smaller details needed in a tight space. We use a rounded cap at all times to work alongside our rounded corner approach.

* Line: accent line:1.5px và basic line: 0.5px
* Stroke: accent stroke:1.5px và basic stroke: 0.5px
* Set round border : Hero size: 1.5px, Spot hero size: 1px, Spot size: 0.5px.

<p className="u-textCenter">
  <img
    src={require('src/assets/structure/stb_illustration_stroke-caps.png')}
    className="u-maxWidthFull"
    style={{ height: 240 }}
    alt="Lines illustrations"
</p>

### Patterns

* Noise
* Line

## Elements

### Character style

<p className="u-textCenter">
  <img
    src={require('src/assets/structure/stb_illustration_human.png')}
    className="u-maxWidthFull"
    style={{ height: 240 }}
    alt="Character illustrations"
</p>

* Human figures not only help tell the story but also build an emotional connection between the product and the users. Characters are styled with exaggerated form by organic shapes. There are a bit over than normal anatomy in the ratio of head and body parts. (Ex: small head with succinct hairstyle, big body with long arms and legs).
* Face expressions: using line to simplify the mouth, nose, eyes and eyebrows.
* Using geometry angles to add movement and motion to the designs.

### Objects

<p className="u-textCenter">
  <img
    src={require('src/assets/structure/stb_illustration_objects.png')}
    className="u-maxWidthFull"
    style={{ height: 240 }}
    alt="Objects illustrations"
</p>

**Detail:**

* Types: office objects, natural objects or animals
* In some cases, objects can be used as the main element of an illustration.

**Background**

* Background types:
  * Fill color shape
  * Decorative objects
* Using Neutral colors for background elements to add high contrast, pay more attention to the main elements.

# Introduction

Source: https://github.com/tutoruniverse/ahaui/blob/main/apps/docs/src/pages/getting-started/introduction.mdx

title: Introduction

# Introduction

<p className="u-text500">Learn how to include Design System in your project</p>

### Installation

The best way to consume Design System is via the npm package which
you can install with `npm` (or `yarn` if you prefer).

```
npm install --save @ahaui/react @ahaui/css
```
or
```
yarn add @ahaui/react @ahaui/css
```

## Stylesheets

And also should import Stylesheets **is required** to use these components.

```js
{/* The following line can be included in your src/index.js or App.js file*/}

import '@ahaui/css/dist/index.min.css';
```

### Importing

You should import individual components like:

```jsx
import { Button } from '@ahaui/react';
```

# Flexbox

Source: https://github.com/tutoruniverse/ahaui/blob/main/apps/docs/src/pages/layout/flex-box.mdx

title: Flex box
import directionRow from 'src/examples/CSS/Flexbox/directionRow';
import directionColumn from 'src/examples/CSS/Flexbox/directionColumn';
import justifyContent from 'src/examples/CSS/Flexbox/justifyContent';
import alignItems from 'src/examples/CSS/Flexbox/alignItems';
import alignSelf from 'src/examples/CSS/Flexbox/alignSelf';
import wrapFlexbox from 'src/examples/CSS/Flexbox/wrap';
import wrapFlexbox2 from 'src/examples/CSS/Flexbox/wrap2';
import alignContent from 'src/examples/CSS/Flexbox/alignContent';
import fillFlexbox from 'src/examples/CSS/Flexbox/fill';
import growFlexbox from 'src/examples/CSS/Flexbox/grow';
import shrinkFlexbox from 'src/examples/CSS/Flexbox/shrink';
import autoMargin from 'src/examples/CSS/Flexbox/autoMargin';
import withAlignItem from 'src/examples/CSS/Flexbox/withAlignItem';
import orderFlexbox from 'src/examples/CSS/Flexbox/order';

# Flexbox

Quickly manage the layout, alignment, and sizing of grid columns, navigation, components, and more with a full suite of responsive flexbox utilities. For more complex implementations, custom CSS may be necessary

## Base

Use `.u-flex` or `.u-flexInline` to enable flex behaviors

<CodeView exampleClassName="example-flexbox" codeText={`<div class="u-flex u-paddingExtraSmall b-highlight">I'm a flexbox container!</div>`}/>
<CodeView exampleClassName="example-flexbox" codeText={`<div class="u-flexInline u-paddingExtraSmall b-highlight">I'm a inline flexbox container!</div>`}/>

## Direction

Use `.u-flexRow` to set a horizontal direction (the browser default), or `.u-flexRowReverse` to start the horizontal direction from the opposite side

<CodeView exampleClassName="example-flexbox" codeText={directionRow}/>

Use `.u-flexColumn` to set a vertical direction, or `.u-flexColumnReverse` to start the vertical direction from the opposite side.

<CodeView exampleClassName="example-flexbox" codeText={directionColumn}/>

## Justify content

Use `.u-justifyContent{X}` on flexbox containers to change the alignment of flex items on the main axis (the x-axis to start, y-axis if flex-direction: column). Choose `X` from Start (browser default), End, Center, Between, or Around.

<CodeView exampleClassName="example-flexbox" codeText={justifyContent}/>

## Align items

Use `.u-alignItems{X}` on flexbox containers to change the alignment of flex items on the cross axis (the x-axis to start, y-axis if flex-direction: column). Choose `X` from Start, End, Center, Baseline, or Stretch(browser default).

<CodeView exampleClassName="example-flexbox" codeText={alignItems}/>

## Align self

Use `.u-alignSelf{X}` on flexbox items to individually change their alignment on the cross axis (the y-axis to start, x-axis if flex-direction: column). Choose `X` from the same options as align-items: Start, End, Center, Baseline, or Stretch (browser default)

<CodeView exampleClassName="example-flexbox" codeText={alignSelf}/>

## Wrap

Change how flex items wrap in a flex container. Choose from no wrapping at all (the browser default) with `.u-flexNoWrap`, wrapping with `.u-flexWrap`, or reverse wrapping with `.u-flexWrapReverse`.

<CodeView exampleClassName="example-flexbox" codeText={wrapFlexbox}/>
<CodeView exampleClassName="example-flexbox" codeText={wrapFlexbox2}/>

## Align content

Use `.u-alignContent{X}` on flexbox containers to align flex items together on the cross axis. Choose `X` from Start (browser default), End, Center, Between, Around, or Stretch. To demonstrate these utilities, we’ve enforced flex-wrap: wrap and increased the number of flex items.

<CodeView exampleClassName="example-flexbox" codeText={alignContent}/>

## Fill

Use the `.u-flexFill` class on a series of sibling elements to force them into widths equal to their content (or equal widths if their content does not surpass their border-boxes) while taking up all available horizontal space.

<CodeView exampleClassName="example-flexbox" codeText={fillFlexbox}/>

## Grow and shrink

Use `.u-flexGrow-*`  utilities to toggle a flex item’s ability to grow to fill available space. In the example below, the `.u-flexGrow1` elements uses all available space it can, while allowing the remaining two flex items their necessary space.

<CodeView exampleClassName="example-flexbox" codeText={growFlexbox}/>

Use `.u-flexShrink-*` utilities to toggle a flex item’s ability to shrink if necessary. In the example below, the second flex item with `.u-flexShrink1` is forced to wrap it’s contents to a new line, “shrinking” to allow more space for the previous flex item with `.u-widthFull`.

<CodeView exampleClassName="example-flexbox" codeText={shrinkFlexbox}/>

## Auto margins

Flexbox can do some pretty awesome things when you mix flex alignments with auto margins. Shown below are three examples of controlling flex items via auto margins: default (no auto margin), pushing two items to the right (`.u-marginRightAuto`), and pushing two items to the left (`.u-marginLeftAuto`).

**Unfortunately, IE10 and IE11 do not properly support auto margins on flex items whose parent has a non-default justify-content value.** See this [StackOverflow answer][1] for more details.

<CodeView exampleClassName="example-flexbox" codeText={autoMargin}/>

## With align-items

Vertically move one flex item to the top or bottom of a container by mixing `align-items`, `flex-direction: column`, and  `margin-top: auto` or `margin-bottom: auto`.

<CodeView exampleClassName="example-flexbox" codeText={withAlignItem}/>

## Order

Change the visual order of specific flex items with a handful of `order` utilities. We only provide options for making an item first or last, as well as a reset to use the DOM order.Choose one of from `.u-flexOrderFirst`, `.u-flexOrderLast`, `.u-flexOrderNone`  (browser default)

<CodeView exampleClassName="example-flexbox" codeText={orderFlexbox}/>

## Responsive classes

The flexbox includes six tiers of predefined classes for building complex responsive layouts. Customize the size of your columns on extra small, small, medium, large, or extra large devices however you see fit.

* `sm:u-X`  - To use at the smallest Media Query breakpoint.
* `md:u-X`  - To use at the medium Media Query breakpoint.
* `lg:u-X`  - To use at the large Media Query breakpoint.
* `xl:u-X`  - To use at the extra large or desktop Media Query breakpoint.
* `xxl:u-X`  - To use at the monitor Media Query breakpoint.

[1]: https://stackoverflow.com/a/37535548

---

# Grid

Source: https://github.com/tutoruniverse/ahaui/blob/main/apps/docs/src/pages/layout/grid.mdx

title: Grid
import examplesColumn10 from 'src/examples/CSS/Grid/10Column';
import examplesColumn12 from 'src/examples/CSS/Grid/12Column';
import removeGutter from 'src/examples/CSS/Grid/removeGutter';
import smallGutter from 'src/examples/CSS/Grid/smallGutter';
import offsetColumn from 'src/examples/CSS/Grid/offsetColumn';

# Grid

Using a grid system is very helpful when designing web pages. It makes it easier to place elements on the page.

## Introduction
The grid system normally has 12 columns (12-column grid system) and has a total width of 100%.

It can also be transformed to other grid systems for the different purposes and layouts, including: 2-column, 3-column, 4-column, 5-column, 6-column, 8-column or 10-column system.

<img
  src={require('src/assets/structure/stb_grid-layout.jpg')}
  srcSet={`${require('src/assets/structure/stb_grid-layout@2x.jpg')} 2x`}
  className="u-maxWidthFull" alt="Grid structure"
<ol className="u-textGray u-marginTopTiny">
  <li>
      Column
  </li>
  <li>
      Region
  </li>
  <li>Gutter</li>
  <li>Row</li>
</ol>

## Setup in Sketch

Step 1: Go to "Layout Settings..."

<p><img src={require('src/assets/sketch-app/grid-settings-menu.jpg')} srcSet={`${require('src/assets/sketch-app/grid-settings-menu@2x.jpg')} 2x`} className="u-maxWidthFull u-border u-rounded" alt="Layout Settings..." /></p>

Step 2: Setup your layout settings according to the following example

<p><img src={require('src/assets/sketch-app/grid-settings.jpg')} srcSet={`${require('src/assets/sketch-app/grid-settings@2x.jpg')} 2x`} className="u-maxWidthFull u-border u-rounded" alt="Layout Settings..." /></p>

## Grid Elements

### Row

A row is the horizontal space which takes 100% of the width, we use Grid to name a row.

Gutter options:

* `Grid`  - has gutter between columns by default
* `Grid--smallGutter`  - small gutter
* `Grid--withoutGutter`  - no gutter

### Column

Column is where to place content. Columns should be placed directly in row. The maximum number of columns in a row is 12. Columns are used withu-size*  in CSS utilities.

#### Sizes

* `u-sizeFit`  - Make an element shrink wrap its content with flex-basis.
* `u-sizeFull`  - Make an element the width of its parent.
* `u-sizeFill`  - Make an element fill the remaining space. Distribute space evenly on multiple elements.
* `u-sizeFillAlt`  - An alternative method to make an element fill the remaining space. Distribute space based on element width.
* `u-sizeXofY`  (numerous) - Specify the proportional width of an object.

`X`  must be an integer less than  `Y`.

`Y`  can be any of the following numbers: 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12.

#### Responsive classes

The grid includes six tiers of predefined classes for building complex responsive layouts. Customize the size of your columns on extra small, small, medium, large, or extra large devices however you see fit.

* `sm:u-sizeXofY`  - To use at the smallest Media Query breakpoint.
* `md:u-sizeXofY`  - To use at the medium Media Query breakpoint.
* `lg:u-sizeXofY`  - To use at the large Media Query breakpoint.
* `xl:u-sizeXofY`  - To use at the extra large or desktop Media Query breakpoint.
* `xxl:u-sizeXofY`  - To use at the monitor Media Query breakpoint.

### Offsetting columns

#### Offset classes

* `u-offsetXofY`  (numerous) - Specify the proportional offset before an object.

#### Responsive classes

The offset includes six tiers of predefined classes for building complex responsive layouts. Customize the size of your columns on extra small, small, medium, large, or extra large devices however you see fit.

* `sm:u-offsetXofY`  - To use at the smallest Media Query breakpoint.
* `md:u-offsetXofY`  - To use at the medium Media Query breakpoint.
* `lg:u-offsetXofY`  - To use at the large Media Query breakpoint.
* `xl:u-offsetXofY`  - To use at the extra large or desktop Media Query breakpoint.
* `xxl:u-offsetXofY`  - To use at the monitor Media Query breakpoint.

## Examples

### 12 columns

<CodeView exampleClassName="example-grids" codeText={examplesColumn12} />

### 10 columns

<CodeView exampleClassName="example-grids" codeText={examplesColumn10} />

### Remove gutter

Use `.Grid--withoutGutter`  to remove a gutter to between cells

<CodeView exampleClassName="example-grids" codeText={removeGutter}/>

### Small gutter

Use  `.Grid--smallGutter`  to add a small gutter to between cells

<CodeView exampleClassName="example-grids" codeText={smallGutter}/>

### Offset columns

<CodeView exampleClassName="example-grids" codeText={offsetColumn}/>

# Split Pane

Source: https://github.com/tutoruniverse/ahaui/blob/main/apps/docs/src/pages/layout/split-pane.mdx

title: Split Pane

# Split Pane

## Introduction

Using the Split Pane component for creating and resizing multi-view layouts. It allows the layouts to be displayed as the viewport width or height increases.

This component is based on [react-split-pane][1]

## Examples

### Horizontal

<CodeView codeText={`
<div className="u-flex u-flexColumn u-paddingExtraSmall u-positionRelative" style={{height:320}}>
  <SplitPane split="horizontal" paneStyle={{
    minHeight: 'calc(30% - 8px)',
    maxHeight: 'calc(70% - 8px'
  }}>
    <div className="u-border u-paddingExtraSmall u-widthFull u-flex u-alignItemsCenter u-justifyContentCenter">Top</div>
    <div className="u-border u-paddingExtraSmall u-widthFull u-heightFull u-flex u-alignItemsCenter u-justifyContentCenter">Bottom</div>
  </SplitPane>
</div>`}

### Vertical

<CodeView codeText={`
<div className="u-flex u-flexColumn u-paddingExtraSmall u-positionRelative" style={{height:320}}>
  <SplitPane split="vertical" paneStyle={{
    minWidth: 'calc(30% - 8px)',
    maxWidth: 'calc(70% - 8px'
  }}>
    <div className="u-border u-paddingExtraSmall  u-heightFull u-widthFull u-flex u-alignItemsCenter u-justifyContentCenter ">Left</div>
    <div className="u-border u-paddingExtraSmall u-widthFull u-heightFull u-flex u-alignItemsCenter u-justifyContentCenter">Right</div>
  </SplitPane>
</div>`}

[1]: https://www.npmjs.com/package/react-split-pane

# Table

Source: https://github.com/tutoruniverse/ahaui/blob/main/apps/docs/src/pages/layout/table.mdx

title: Table
import defaultTable from 'src/examples/CSS/Table/default';
import stickyHeaderTable from 'src/examples/CSS/Table/stickyHeader';

import borderedTable from 'src/examples/CSS/Table/bordered';
import hoverableTable from 'src/examples/CSS/Table/hoverable';
import narrowTable from 'src/examples/CSS/Table/narrow';
import smallTable from 'src/examples/CSS/Table/small';

# Table

## Introduction

Due to the widespread use of tables across third-party widgets like calendars and date pickers, we’ve designed our tables to be opt-in. Just add the base class  .Table to any `<table>`, then extend with custom styles or our various included modifier classes.

Responsive tables
Tables can be responsive by adding these CSS classes into their parent elements:
`.u-block .u-widthFull .u-overflowHorizontalAuto`

## Examples
### Default

Default style with white background and no border.

<CodeView codeText={defaultTable}/>

### Sticky Header

Fixed the header on top of the table during the vertical scrolling.

<CodeView codeText={stickyHeaderTable}/>

### Striped

Easy to see with odd and even rows styles.

<CodeView codeText={stripedTable}/>

### Bordered

Box the table with its border.

<CodeView codeText={borderedTable}/>

### Hoverable

With background when hover.

<CodeView codeText={hoverableTable}/>

### Narrow

Reduce the cells' padding.

<CodeView codeText={narrowTable}/>

### Small

Smaller font size and cells' padding.

<CodeView codeText={smallTable}/>
